title.zh: 卷七十七 列傳第四十七 陸曄 何充 褚翜 蔡謨 諸葛恢 殷浩
title.en: Volume 77 Biographies 47: Lu Ye; He Chong; Chu Se; Cai Mo; Zhuge Hui; Yin Hao
title.raw: 卷七十七 列傳第四十七 陸曄 何充 褚翜 蔡謨 諸葛恢 殷浩 Volume 77 Biographies 47: Lu Ye; He Chong; Chu Se; Cai Mo; Zhuge Hui; Yin Hao

sentences.zh: 陸曄，字士光，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Ye, courtesy name Shiguang, was a man of Wu in the Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ye, courtesy Shiguang, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 伯父喜，吳吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Xi was Minister of the Ministry of Personnel of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Lu Xi had served as Wu's minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 父英，高平相，員外散騎常侍，曄少有雅望，從兄機每稱之曰：「我家世不乏公矣。

translations.literal: His father Ying was chancellor of Gaoping and supernumerary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary. Ye from youth had a reputation for cultivated dignity; his elder patriline cousin Ji would often praise him, saying, "In our house for generations we have not lacked for dukes."
translations.idiomatic: His father Lu Ying had been chancellor of Gaoping and supernumerary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary. Even as a young man Lu Ye was esteemed for poise and dignity; his older cousin Lu Ji used to say of him, "Our family has never wanted for men fit to be dukes."

sentences.zh: 」居喪，以孝聞。

translations.literal: " After he observed mourning, he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When he observed mourning for his parents, his filial devotion became widely known.

sentences.zh: 同郡顧榮與鄉人書曰：「士光氣息裁屬，慮其性命，言之傷心矣。

translations.literal: Gu Rong of the same commandery wrote in a letter to fellow townsmen, saying, "Shiguang's breath barely holds together; I worry for his life—speaking of it wounds the heart."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong, also from Wu commandery, wrote to friends at home: "Shiguang is so weak he can scarcely draw breath; I fear for his life—and it breaks my heart to speak of it."

sentences.zh: 」後察孝廉，除永世、烏江二縣令，皆不就。

translations.literal: " Later he was examined and recommended as filially incorrupt; he was appointed magistrate of the two counties Yongshi and Wujiang, but in neither case did he take office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recommended on the filial-incorrupt roll and offered the magistracies of Yongshi and Wujiang; he declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 元帝初鎮江左，辟為祭酒，尋補振威將軍、義興太守，以疾不拜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan first established his base east of the Yangzi, Ye was summoned as libationer; shortly he was additionally appointed general who rouses might and administrator of Yixing, but because of illness he did not assume office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan first took up his seat east of the Yangzi, Lu Ye was called to serve as libationer; he was soon named general who rouses might and governor of Yixing, but illness kept him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 預討華軼功，封平望亭侯，累遷散騎常侍、本郡大中正。

translations.literal: For merit in joining the campaign against Hua Yi he was enfeoffed village marquis of Pingwang, and by stages was promoted to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and senior rectifier of his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a share of the credit for the expedition against Hua Yi and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Pingwang; he rose step by step to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and senior rectifier for his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 太興元年，遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixing he was transferred to household supervisor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 318 he was appointed supervisor of the household of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 時帝以侍中皆北士，宜兼用南人，曄以清貞著稱，遂拜侍中，徙尚書，領州大中正。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor considered that the attendants-in-ordinary were all northerners and that southerners ought also to be employed; Ye was famed for purity and integrity, so he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary, transferred to the secretariat, and concurrently served as senior rectifier of the province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor felt that the attendants-in-ordinary were drawn too exclusively from northern families and that southerners should be brought in as well. Lu Ye was known for spotless integrity, so he was named attendant-in-ordinary, moved to a secretariat post, and made senior rectifier for the province.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，轉光祿勳，遷太常，代紀瞻為尚書左僕射，領太子少傅，尋加金紫光祿大夫，代卞壼為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Ye was transferred to chamberlain for the palace revenues, then moved to grand astrologer; he replaced Ji Zhan as left vice director of the secretariat, concurrent junior tutor to the heir apparent; shortly he was given the added title cavalier supervisor of the household, gold and purple, and replaced Bian Kun as general who commands the army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served as chamberlain for the palace revenues, then as grand astrologer; he succeeded Ji Zhan as left vice director of the secretariat while also serving as junior tutor to the heir apparent, and soon received the gold-and-purple cavalier supervisor title before replacing Bian Kun as commanding general of the imperial guards.

sentences.zh: 以平錢鳳功，進爵江陵伯。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Qian Feng his noble rank was advanced to earl of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in defeating Qian Feng he was advanced in rank to earl of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，曄與王導、壼、庾亮、溫嶠、郗鑒並受顧命，輔皇太子，更入殿將兵直宿。

translations.literal: When the emperor was gravely ill, Ye together with Wang Dao, Kun, Yu Liang, Wen Qiao, and Xi Jian jointly received testamentary charge, assisted the heir apparent, and in rotation entered the halls leading troops for night duty.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor lay dying, Lu Ye joined Wang Dao, Bian Kun, Yu Liang, Wen Qiao, and Xi Jian in receiving the deathbed commission to assist the heir apparent; they took turns entering the palace at the head of troops and standing night watch.

sentences.zh: 遺詔曰：「曄清操忠貞，曆職顯允，且其兄弟事君如父，憂國如家，歲寒不凋，體自門風。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict said, "Ye is pure in conduct and loyal in devotion; in successive offices he has been conspicuously trustworthy, and moreover he and his brothers serve the ruler as a father and worry for the state as for their own family—they do not wither in the cold of the year; such is the temper of their gate and lineage."
translations.idiomatic: The testamentary edict read: "Lu Ye is upright, loyal, and trustworthy in every post he has held; he and his brothers serve their sovereign as they would a father and care for the state as they would their own household—they keep faith when times turn harsh. That steadfastness is the very stamp of their line."

sentences.zh: 既委以六軍，可錄尚書事，加散騎常侍。」

translations.literal: Having already entrusted him with the six armies, he may record overseer business for the secretariat, with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary."
translations.idiomatic: The six armies are already in his hands; let him take charge of recording overseer business for the secretariat and add the title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary."

sentences.zh: 成帝踐阼，拜左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，給親兵百人，常侍如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, Ye was appointed left grand household, bearer of the golden seal and purple ribbon, with a hundred picked troops as his bodyguard; his post as attendant-in-ordinary remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng came to the throne, Lu Ye was named left grand household with the full ceremonial privileges of the three excellencies, given a hundred household guards, and kept on as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之難，曄隨帝左石頭，舉動方正，不以凶威變節。

translations.literal: During the troubles of Su Jun, Ye followed the sovereign to Stone Fort; his bearing showed firm rectitude, and he did not alter his integrity before savage intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's revolt Lu Ye stayed with the emperor at the Stone fortress; he carried himself with unbending dignity and refused to bend his principles to brute force.

sentences.zh: 峻以曄吳士之望，不敢加害，使守留台。

translations.literal: Because Jun considered Ye the hope of Wu gentry, he did not dare harm him and had him guard the rear secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun dared not harm him, knowing Lu Ye stood for the southern elite of Wu, and instead put him in charge of the rear secretariat.

sentences.zh: 匡術以苑城歸順，時共推曄督宮城軍事。

translations.literal: When Kuang Shu surrendered Yuancheng to allegiance, at the time they jointly urged Ye to supervise military affairs of the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuang Shu came over from Yuancheng with his garrison, the court leaders together asked Lu Ye to direct military operations inside the palace enclosure.

sentences.zh: 峻平，加衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified, Ye was given the added title general who guards the guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun's defeat Lu Ye received the additional title general who guards the guard.

sentences.zh: 給千兵百騎，以勳進爵為公，封次子嘏新康子。

translations.literal: He was granted a thousand foot soldiers and a hundred horsemen; for merit his noble rank was advanced to duke, and his second son Gu was enfeoffed baron of Xinkang.
translations.idiomatic: He was allotted a thousand infantry and a hundred cavalry; his noble rank was raised to duke for distinguished service, and his second son, Lu Gu, was enfeoffed as baron of Xinkang.

sentences.zh: 咸和中，求歸鄉里拜墳墓。

translations.literal: In the Xianhe era he requested to return to his home village to pay respects at tombs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianhe years he asked leave to go home and tend his family's graves.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，舊制假六十日。

translations.literal: The relevant office reported that according to old regulations leave was granted for sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials reported that precedent allowed sixty days' leave for the purpose.

sentences.zh: 侍中顏含、黃門侍郎馮懷駁曰：「曄內蘊至德，清一其心，受託付之重，居台司之位，既蒙詔許歸省填塋，大臣之義本在忘己，豈容有期而反，無期必遠。

translations.literal: Yan Han, attendant-in-ordinary, and Feng Huai, gentleman attendant at the yellow gates, objected, saying, "Ye harbors consummate virtue within and keeps his heart utterly pure; he bears the weight of a regent's charge and holds ministerial rank. Since he has already received imperial permission to return and inspect his family's tombs, the righteousness of a great minister fundamentally lies in forgetting self—how can one allow a fixed term for return, and if there were no fixed term he would surely linger far away?"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Yan Han and gentleman attendant at the yellow gates Feng Huai objected: "Lu Ye embodies the highest virtue and keeps his mind unclouded; he carries a regent's burden and sits at the summit of government. The throne has already granted him leave to visit his ancestors' graves. A great minister's duty is to forget himself—how can we tie him to a deadline for coming back, or, with no deadline, watch him stay away indefinitely?"

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜還自還，不須制日。

translations.literal: We foolishly consider that he should return when he returns of himself, without prescribing days.
translations.idiomatic: We submit that he should be left to return in his own time, without a fixed limit on his stay.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，曄因歸。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this, and Ye therefore returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Lu Ye went home on those terms.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: He died of illness at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、車騎大將軍，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded attendant-in-ordinary and grand general who commands chariots and cavalry; his posthumous name was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as attendant-in-ordinary and grand general of chariots and cavalry, with the posthumous epithet Mu, "Solemn."

sentences.zh: 子諶，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Chen was cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lu Chen rose to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 玩字士瑤。

translations.literal: Wan had the courtesy name Shiyao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan's courtesy name was Shiyao.

sentences.zh: 器量淹雅，弱冠有美名，賀循每稱其清允平當，郡檄綱紀，東海王越辟為掾，皆不就。

translations.literal: Of broad capacity and refined elegance, while still in the weak-capped years he had a fine reputation; He Xun always praised his purity, trustworthiness, and even balance. He was summoned by commandery dispatch as local registrar, and Prince of Donghai Yue summoned him as clerk—he took neither post.
translations.idiomatic: He was magnanimous and cultivated, and even before his capping at twenty he was already well spoken of. He Xun often praised his clarity, honesty, and even temper. The commandery tried to appoint him chief clerk; Sima Yue, prince of Donghai, invited him onto his staff—but Lu Wan refused every summons.

sentences.zh: 元帝引為丞相參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan brought him in as adjutant to the chancellor's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan then brought him in as an adjutant on the chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 時王導初至江左，思結人情，請婚於玩。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Dao had just arrived east of the Yangzi and wished to secure men's goodwill; he requested a marriage alliance with Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao had only lately crossed the Yangzi and was eager to win local support; he asked to seal an alliance by marrying into Lu Wan's family.

sentences.zh: 玩對曰：「培塿無松柏，薰蕕不同器。

translations.literal: Wan replied, saying, "On a small mound there are no pine or cypress; mugwort and thoroughwort are not placed in the same vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan answered: "You do not plant pine and cypress on a little hillock, and sweet grass does not share a vessel with stinking rue."

sentences.zh: 玩雖不才，義不能為亂倫之始。

translations.literal: Though Wan lacks talent, in righteousness he cannot be the one who begins disorder in proper relations.
translations.idiomatic: I am no man of parts, but I cannot in good conscience be the first to break the proper order between our houses.

sentences.zh: 」導乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Dao desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 玩嘗詣導食酪，因而得疾。

translations.literal: Wan once visited Dao and ate curdled milk, and on account of this fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On one visit to Wang Dao, Lu Wan was served fermented milk and fell ill from it.

sentences.zh: 與導箋曰：「僕雖吳人，幾為傖鬼。

translations.literal: In a note to Dao he said, "Though I am a man of Wu, I was nearly made a ghost of your milk-drinking northerners."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Dao a note: "I may be a southerner, but that meal nearly turned me into a ghost of your northern ways."

sentences.zh: 」其輕易權貴如此。

translations.literal: " In this way he treated the mighty with levity.
translations.idiomatic: That was the tone—easy and irreverent—in which he addressed the powerful.

sentences.zh: 累加奮武將軍，徵拜侍中，以疾辭。

translations.literal: By stages he was given the added title general who exerts martial might; he was summoned and appointed attendant-in-ordinary, but declined because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who exerts martial might and summoned to the post of attendant-in-ordinary, which he declined on grounds of ill health.

sentences.zh: 王敦請為長史，逼以軍期，不得已，乃從命。

translations.literal: Wang Dun requested him as chief clerk, pressing him with military deadlines; having no choice, he then obeyed the order.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun pressed him to serve as chief clerk, backing the demand with military deadlines; Lu Wan had no choice but to comply.

sentences.zh: 敦平，尚書令郗鑒議敦佐吏不能匡正奸惡，宜皆免官禁錮。

translations.literal: When Dun was pacified, Xi Jian, grand director of the secretariat, proposed that Dun's staff officers, being unable to correct wickedness, ought all to be dismissed from office and forbidden from service.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's defeat, grand director of the secretariat Xi Jian argued that Dun's aides had failed to restrain his treason and should all be cashiered and barred from office.

sentences.zh: 會溫嶠上表申理，得不坐。

translations.literal: As it happened Wen Qiao submitted a memorial arguing their case, so they did not suffer punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao then submitted a memorial in their defense, and the penalty was not applied.

sentences.zh: 復拜侍中，遷吏部尚書，領會稽王師，讓不拜，轉尚書左僕射，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: He was again appointed attendant-in-ordinary, promoted to minister of the ministry of personnel, concurrent tutor to the prince of Kuaiji—he declined and did not take office—was transferred to left vice director of the secretariat, concurrent senior rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named attendant-in-ordinary and promoted to minister of personnel with concurrent appointment as tutor to the prince of Kuaiji, which he refused; he was then made left vice director of the secretariat while continuing as senior rectifier for his native province.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻反，遣玩與兄曄俱守宮城。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, he sent Wan together with his elder brother Ye jointly to defend the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rose in revolt, Lu Wan was ordered to defend the palace city alongside his elder brother Lu Ye.

sentences.zh: 玩潛說匡術歸順，以功封興平伯。

translations.literal: Wan secretly persuaded Kuang Shu to submit to allegiance; for merit he was enfeoffed baron of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan quietly persuaded Kuang Shu to come over to the throne; for that service he was enfeoffed as baron of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「玩體道清純，雅量弘遠，歷位內外，風績顯著。

translations.literal: Again an edict said, "Wan embodies the Way in purity; his cultivated capacity is broad and far-reaching; in successive posts inside and outside his repute and achievement have been conspicuous."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "Lu Wan cleaves to the Way with unmixed purity; his breadth of mind is exceptional; in every office, civil or military, his record shines."

sentences.zh: 宜居台司，以允眾望。

translations.literal: He ought to occupy ministerial rank, so as to satisfy the multitude's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He belongs in the highest councils of state, where the realm's expectations can rest on him."

sentences.zh: 授左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，餘如故。

translations.literal: Appoint him left grand household, bearer of the golden seal and purple ribbon, with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; the remainder as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be appointed left grand household with the full honors of the three excellencies, and add the title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; his other duties remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 」玩頻自表，優詔褒揚。

translations.literal: " Wan repeatedly memorialized on his own behalf; cordial edicts praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan sent memorial after memorial declining the honor; the throne answered with warm edicts of praise.

sentences.zh: 重復自陳曰：「臣實凡短，風操不立，階緣嘉會，便蕃榮顯，遂總括憲台，豫聞政道。

translations.literal: Again he personally stated, saying, "Your servant is truly mean and short of stature; moral bearing I have not established; only by stepping on a fortunate meeting have I repeatedly enjoyed glory and honor, until I came to oversee the censorate in summary fashion and share in hearing of the way of government."
translations.idiomatic: He laid out his case again: "I am a man of modest gifts who has never forged a reputation for integrity; sheer good fortune has raised me again and again until I preside over the censorate and take part in shaping policy."

sentences.zh: 竟不能敷融玄風，清一朝序，咎責之來，於臣已重。

translations.literal: In the end I have been unable to diffuse and blend the subtle breeze of the teaching nor bring clarity to a court's ordering; as blame comes, for your servant it is already heavy.
translations.idiomatic: I have failed to spread the transforming influence of good government or to bring order to the court; if fault is to be found, I have already borne more than my share."

sentences.zh: 誠以身許國，義忘曲讓。

translations.literal: Truly I vowed my person to the state; in duty I forgot private pride.
translations.idiomatic: I have given myself wholly to the state and set private pride aside."

sentences.zh: 而慺慺所守，終於陳訴者，特以端右機要，事務殷多，臣已盈六十之年，智力有限，疾患深重，體氣日弊，朝夕自勵，非復所堪。

translations.literal: Yet what I earnestly insist on and finally lay before you in petition is solely because the posts at the right are crucial and affairs are numerous; your servant has already passed sixty years; intelligence and strength are limited; illness is deep and grave; bodily vigor daily fails; though morning and evening I steel myself, I can no longer bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I press this appeal because the senior posts at court are the pivot of power and their burden is crushing: I am past sixty, my strength and judgment are limited, my illness grows worse by the day, and I am no longer equal to the task no matter how hard I drive myself.

sentences.zh: 若偃息苟免，職事並廢，則莫大之悔，天下將謂臣何！

translations.literal: If I rest easy and merely seek to escape blame, and office and duty together lapse, then what regret could be greater, and what will the realm say of your servant!
translations.idiomatic: If I stayed on only to save myself while duty collapsed around me, the shame would be beyond measure—what would the world think of me then?"

sentences.zh: 乞陛下披豁聖懷，霈然垂允。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to open wide your sagely heart and let your grace rain down and grant assent.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to open your heart and grant this relief in full measure."

sentences.zh: 」詔不許。

translations.literal: " The edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused his request.

sentences.zh: 玩重表曰：「臣比披誠款，不足上暢天聰，聖恩徘徊，厲以體國。

translations.literal: Wan again memorialized, saying, "Your servant of late has spread sincerity and earnestness, insufficient to ascend and reach Heaven's hearing; Your Majesty's kindness lingers, sternly charging me to think of the body politic."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan submitted another memorial: "I have laid my sincerity before you, yet it has not risen to your ears; your kindness still holds me back with stern reminders to think of the realm as a whole."

sentences.zh: 臣聞至公之道，上下玄同，用才不負其長，量力不受其短。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in the way of utmost fairness high and low merge in darkness; one employs talent without burdening it beyond its strengths, and measures strength without taking on what exceeds one's limits.
translations.idiomatic: They say the path of perfect equity joins ruler and subject in a single purpose: talents are used without asking more of them than they can give, and offices are not piled on men beyond their strength."

sentences.zh: 雖加官重祿無世不有，皆庸勳親賢，時所須賴，兼統以濟世務，非優崇以榮一人。

translations.literal: Though offices weighted with salary and rank have existed in no age without them, they have all been for ordinary merit and close kin whom the times truly need—joint oversight to help the age's tasks, not preferential elevation to honor a single man.
translations.idiomatic: High rank and rich stipends exist in every reign, but they are meant for proven merit and trusted kin whom the age cannot do without—shared responsibility for the common good, not private glory for one man."

sentences.zh: 臣受遇三世，恩隆寵厚，豈敢辭職事之勞，求沖讓之譽。

translations.literal: Your servant has received favor through three reigns; kindness is rich and favor thick—how dare I decline the toil of office to seek a reputation for lofty modesty?
translations.idiomatic: I have enjoyed favor under three sovereigns, with kindness and honors beyond desert—how could I shirk real work merely to win a name for modesty?"

sentences.zh: 徒以端右要重，興替所存，久以無任，妨賢曠職。

translations.literal: Only because the posts at the right are vital, where rise and fall are stored, long I have been unfit, obstructing worthies and leaving office vacant.
translations.idiomatic: I speak only because these senior posts govern success or failure at court, and I have long been unfit to hold them—blocking better men while the office lies empty."

sentences.zh: 臣猶自知不可，況天下之人乎！

translations.literal: Your servant alone still knows I cannot do it—how much less the men of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: If I know I am not equal to the task, how much more must everyone else!"

sentences.zh: 今復外參論道，內統百揆，不堪之名，有如皎日。

translations.literal: Now again to advise on the Way abroad and hold the hundred handles within, the name of being unfit is like the bright sun.
translations.idiomatic: To counsel on the great principles abroad and direct every branch of government within—my unfitness for that role is as plain as the noonday sun."

sentences.zh: 願陛下少垂哀矜，使四海知官不可以私於人，人不可以私取官，則天工弘坦，誰不謂允！

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would show a little pity, so that within the four seas men may know offices may not be given through private favor to men, and men may not through private favor grasp offices—then Heaven's workmanship will be broad and level, and who will not call it fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Show a little mercy, so that all within the four seas may see that office is not a private gift and that men ought not privately seize power—then the kingly work will stand open and fair, and who could call that wrong?"

sentences.zh: 」猶不許。

translations.literal: " Still permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Again the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 尋而王導、郗鑒、庾亮相繼而薨，朝野咸以為三良既沒，國家殄瘁。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wang Dao, Xi Jian, and Yu Liang in succession died; court and countryside alike considered that three good men had already perished and the state was withered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Dao, Xi Jian, and Yu Liang died one after another; court and country alike felt that three pillars of the state were gone and the dynasty had been left desolate.

sentences.zh: 以玩有德望，乃遷侍中、司空，給羽林四十人。

translations.literal: Because Wan had virtue and prestige, he was then moved to attendant-in-ordinary and minister of works, with forty guards of the feathery forest granted.
translations.idiomatic: On account of Lu Wan's moral authority he was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and minister of works, with a guard of forty picked troops from the feathery forest.

sentences.zh: 玩既拜，有人詣之，索杯酒，瀉置柱梁之間，咒曰：「當今乏材，以爾為柱石，莫傾人梁棟邪！

translations.literal: When Wan had taken office, someone visited him, asked for a cup of wine, poured it in the space between pillar and beam, and cursed, saying, "In this age talent is lacking, and they make you their pillar and stone—will you not topple the people's beams and ridgepoles!"
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Wan had received appointment, a caller asked for a cup of wine, poured it between a pillar and its tie-beam, and swore: "The age is short of timber, yet they make you their mainstay—are you trying to bring the roof down on us?"

sentences.zh: 」玩笑曰：「戢卿良箴。

translations.literal: " Wan said with a smile, "I will restrain myself to your good admonition."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan smiled and said, "I shall take your wise counsel to heart."

sentences.zh: 」既而歎息，謂賓客曰：「以我為三公，是天下為無人。

translations.literal: " Then he sighed and told his guests, "Taking me as one of the three dukes means the realm has no men."
translations.idiomatic: Then he sighed and told his guests, "If they can make me one of the three excellencies, the realm must truly be out of men."

sentences.zh: 」談者以為知言。

translations.literal: " Discussants considered this knowledgeable speech.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard the remark judged it penetrating.

sentences.zh: 玩雖登公輔，謙讓不辟掾屬。

translations.literal: Though Wan had ascended to senior minister, in modesty he did not summon subordinate clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Lu Wan rose to chief minister, he modestly refused to appoint a private staff.

sentences.zh: 成帝聞而勸之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng heard of it, he urged him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng heard of this and urged him to relent.

sentences.zh: 玩不得已而從命，所辟皆寒素有行之士。

translations.literal: Wan having no choice obeyed the order; those he summoned were all men of humble pedigree but of proven conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan yielded at last; every man he brought on was of humble birth but solid character.

sentences.zh: 玩翼亮累世，常以弘重為人主所貴，加性通雅，不以名位格物，誘納後進，謙若布衣，由是搢紳之徒莫不廕其德宇。

translations.literal: Through successive reigns Wan gave steady assistance; he was always prized by rulers for his solemn weight, and moreover his nature was broad and cultivated—he did not use name or office to relegate others, enticed and received those who came after, and humbled himself like a common scholar; therefore gentry of the sash never failed to shelter in the canopy of his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan had steadied the throne through reign after reign; sovereigns valued his gravity and breadth, and his manner was open and refined—he never pulled rank, welcomed younger men, and carried himself with the modesty of a private scholar, so that the whole gentry class basked in his moral presence.

sentences.zh: 後疾甚，上表曰：「臣嬰遘疾疢，沈頓曆月，不蒙痊損，而日夕漸篤，自省微綿，無復生望。

translations.literal: Later when his illness was grave, he submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has long been encumbered with disease and affliction, sunk in prostration for months; I have not received restoration to health, but day and night it gradually worsens; examining myself, my thread of life is slight; I have no further hope of life."
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew severe he presented a memorial: "For months I have been laid low by sickness without improvement; each day leaves me weaker, and I no longer expect to live."

sentences.zh: 荷恩不報，孤負已及，仰瞻天覆，伏枕隕涕。

translations.literal: Having received favor yet not repaying it, I have failed those who trusted me; I lift my eyes to Heaven's covering and weep, prostrate on the pillow.
translations.idiomatic: I have received grace I cannot repay, and I have failed those who trusted me; I lift my eyes to Heaven's canopy and weep into my pillow."

sentences.zh: 臣年向中壽，窮極寵榮，終身歸全，將復何恨！

translations.literal: Your servant's years approach middle span of life; I have exhausted favor and glory; to end my person whole—what further regret could there be!
translations.idiomatic: I have reached the years men call middle age and have tasted every honor the throne can give; if I may end my days with body whole, what more could I ask?"

sentences.zh: 惟願陛下崇明聖德，弘敷洪化，曾構祖宗之基，道濟群生之命。

translations.literal: Only I pray that Your Majesty will clarify and make bright sagely virtue, spread in breadth the great transformation, enlarge the foundation built by the ancestors, and by the Way ford the lives of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Only let Your Majesty refine your sacred virtue, extend your transforming influence far and wide, deepen the foundations your ancestors laid, and bring the Way to bear on the lives of all your people."

sentences.zh: 臣不勝臨命遺戀之情，貪及視息，上表以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant cannot master the feeling of parting grief at the end of life; greedy only for the breath in my eyes, I submit this memorial that it may be heard.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot master the grief of this final parting; while I still have sight and breath I lay this memorial before you."

sentences.zh: 」薨年六十四，諡曰康，給兵千人，守塚七十家。

translations.literal: " He died at age sixty-four; his posthumous name was Kang; a thousand soldiers were granted, and seventy households to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four and received the posthumous epithet Kang, "At ease"; a thousand soldiers were assigned to his tomb, with seventy households to maintain it.

sentences.zh: 太元中，功臣普被減削，司空何充等止得六家，以玩有佐命之勳，先陪陵而葬，由是特置興平伯官屬以衛墓。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan period, merit nobles were generally subjected to reduction and cutting; Minister of Works He Chong and others received only six households, but because Wan had merit as supporter of the founding mandate and had been buried first accompanying the tombs, on this account there was specially established the establishment of a baron of Xingping's officials to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan era merit nobles everywhere saw their hereditary privileges trimmed; even Minister of Works He Chong was left with only six tomb-keeping households. Because Lu Wan had helped establish the dynasty and lay buried beside the imperial mausoleum belt, a special baronial establishment was retained at Xingping to guard his grave.

sentences.zh: 子始嗣，曆侍中、尚書。

translations.literal: His son Shi succeeded him; he passed through attendant-in-ordinary and the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lu Shi inherited the title and went on to serve as attendant-in-ordinary and in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 玩子納

translations.literal: Wan's son Na.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan's son Lu Na

sentences.zh: 納字祖言。

translations.literal: Na had the courtesy name Zuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na, courtesy Zuyan

sentences.zh: 少有清操，貞厲絕俗。

translations.literal: From youth he had pure conduct, stern integrity cutting him off from the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was known for spotless conduct and a severity of principle that set him apart from the common run.

sentences.zh: 初辟鎮軍大將軍、武陵王掾，州舉秀才。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned as clerk to the general who guards the army, Prince of Wuling, and the province nominated him flourishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a clerk on the staff of the general who guards the army, the prince of Wuling, and the province nominated him as a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 太原王述雅敬重之，引為建威長史。

translations.literal: Wang Shu of Taiyuan, famed for esteeming him, brought him in as chief clerk to general who establishes might.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu of Taiyuan, who admired him greatly, brought him in as chief clerk to the general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門侍郎、本州別駕、尚書吏部郎，出為吳興太守。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted to gentleman at the yellow gates, provincial administrator on separate carriage for his home province, director in the ministry of personnel of the secretariat, and went out as administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through gentleman at the yellow gates, chief administrator on the staff of his home province, and director in the ministry of personnel before being sent out as governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 將之郡，先至姑孰辭桓溫，因問溫曰：「公致醉可飲幾酒？

translations.literal: When about to go to the commandery, he first arrived at Gushu to take leave of Huan Wen, and therefore asked Wen, saying, "When you allow yourself to become drunk, how much wine can you drink?"
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving for his commandery he stopped at Gushu to bid Huan Wen farewell and asked him, "When you mean to drink yourself drunk, how much wine does it take?"

sentences.zh: 食肉多少？

translations.literal: How much meat do you eat?
translations.idiomatic: How much meat do you eat?"

sentences.zh: 」溫曰：「年大來飲三升便醉，白肉不過十臠。

translations.literal: " Wen said, "In old age I drink three sheng and then am drunk; plain meat I take in no more than ten slices."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen replied, "These days three pints of wine are enough to lay me out, and I take no more than ten slices of plain meat."

sentences.zh: 卿復云何？

translations.literal: And how is it with you?
translations.idiomatic: What about you?

sentences.zh: 」納曰：「素不能飲，止可二升，肉亦不足言。

translations.literal: " Na said, "By nature I cannot drink—only two sheng; as for meat, it is not worth speaking of."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na said, "I have never been able to drink—two pints at most—and the meat hardly bears mentioning."

sentences.zh: 」後伺溫閑，謂之曰：「外有微禮，方守遠郡，欲與公一醉，以展下情。

translations.literal: " Later, catching Wen at leisure, he said to him, "Outside there is a modest gift; I am about to hold a distant commandery; I wish with you to get drunk once, so as to unfold humble feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he found Huan Wen at leisure, he said, "I have a small gift outside; I am bound for a distant post and should like to drink you under the table once, if I may, as a mark of regard."

sentences.zh: 」溫欣然納之。

translations.literal: " Wen gladly accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen accepted with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 時王坦之、刁彝在坐。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Tanzhi and Diao Yi were seated with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi and Diao Yi were present.

sentences.zh: 及受禮，唯酒一斗，鹿肉一拌，坐客愕然。

translations.literal: When the gift was received, there was only one dou of wine and one bowl of deer meat; the seated guests were stunned.
translations.idiomatic: When the "gift" arrived it proved to be a single measure of wine and one platter of venison; the guests sat dumbstruck.

sentences.zh: 納徐曰：「明公近雲飲酒三升，納止可二升，今有一斗，以備杯杓餘瀝。

translations.literal: Na slowly said, "The gentleman lately said that when drunk you drink three sheng; I can manage only two sheng; now there is one dou of wine to supply the lees left in cups and ladles."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na said evenly, "You told me yourself that three pints get you drunk and I can manage only two; I have brought a full gallon so there will be something left in the cups after we pour."

sentences.zh: 」溫及賓客並歎其率素，更敕中廚設精饌，酣飲極歎而罷。

translations.literal: Wen together with the guests all sighed at his plain candor; again he ordered the inner kitchen to set out fine dishes, and they drank deep in admiration until they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen and his guests marveled at his blunt honesty; Huan then ordered the kitchen to lay out a proper feast, and they drank their fill in high good humor.

sentences.zh: 納至郡，不受俸祿。

translations.literal: When Na arrived at the commandery, he did not accept salary or stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed in his commandery, Lu Na refused to draw his official salary.

sentences.zh: 頃之，徵拜左民尚書，領州大中正。

translations.literal: Shortly he was summoned and appointed minister of the left people, concurrent senior rectifier of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as minister for the common people while continuing as senior rectifier for the province.

sentences.zh: 將應召，外白宜裝幾船，納曰：「私奴裝糧食來，無所復須也。

translations.literal: When about to answer the summons, those outside reported how many boats ought to be loaded; Na said, "My private slaves are bringing grain; nothing further is needed."
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to leave for the capital, his staff asked how many riverboats should be fitted out. He replied, "My household slaves are already shipping my grain—nothing more is required."

sentences.zh: 」臨發，止有被襆而已，其餘並封以還官。

translations.literal: At the time of departure he had only a bundled quilt; the rest he sealed and returned to the office.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out he carried nothing but a quilt roll; everything else he sealed up and sent back to the yamen.

sentences.zh: 遷太常，徙吏部尚書，加奉車都尉、衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to grand astrologer, transferred to minister of personnel, with the added titles colonel who follows the carriage and general who guards the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand astrologer, then minister of personnel, with the added titles colonel who follows the carriage and general who guards the guard.

sentences.zh: 謝安嘗欲詣納，而納殊無供辦。

translations.literal: Xie An once wished to visit Na, but Na had made no preparations whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An once planned a call on Lu Na, who had made no arrangements to receive him.

sentences.zh: 其兄子俶不敢問之，乃密為之具。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Shu did not dare ask him, and secretly prepared for him.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Lu Shu dared not question him and quietly laid in supplies behind his back.

sentences.zh: 安既至，納所設唯茶果而已。

translations.literal: When An had arrived, what Na had set out was only tea and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie An arrived, Lu Na offered nothing but tea and fruit.

sentences.zh: 俶遂陳盛饌，珍羞畢具。

translations.literal: Shu then spread out a lavish feast, with rare delicacies all provided.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shu then produced a lavish spread of every costly delicacy.

sentences.zh: 客罷，納大怒曰：「汝不能光益父叔，乃復穢我素業邪！

translations.literal: When the guests left, Na raged, saying, "You cannot bring lustre to your father and uncles, and would again defile my plain livelihood!"
translations.idiomatic: After the guests had gone, Lu Na flared up: "You cannot add honor to your father and uncles—must you also smear my plain way of life?"

sentences.zh: 」於是杖之四十。

translations.literal: Thereupon he caned him forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He had him flogged forty blows.

sentences.zh: 其舉措多此類。

translations.literal: His conduct was mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His behavior was habitually of that kind.

sentences.zh: 後以愛子長生有疾，求解官營視，兄子禽又犯法應刑，乞免官謝罪。

translations.literal: Later because his beloved son Changsheng was ill, he requested to resign office to tend him; his elder brother's son Qin also violated the law and faced punishment, and he begged to resign office to acknowledge guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his favorite son Changsheng fell ill, he asked leave to quit office and nurse him; his nephew Qin had also broken the law and faced the death penalty, so he offered to resign and accept blame.

sentences.zh: 詔特許輕降。

translations.literal: An edict specially permitted a light reduction of penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted a special mitigation of the penalties involved.

sentences.zh: 頃長生小佳，喻還攝職。

translations.literal: Shortly Changsheng improved a little; he was instructed to return and resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Changsheng rallied slightly, the court told Lu Na to resume his post.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書僕射，轉左僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to vice director of the secretariat, transferred to left vice director, with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice director of the secretariat, then left vice director, with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 俄拜尚書令，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed grand director of the secretariat; attendant-in-ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became grand director of the secretariat while keeping his cavalier attendant post.

sentences.zh: 恪勤貞固，始終不渝。

translations.literal: He was diligent, steadfast, and loyal from first to last without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: He was tireless, upright, and utterly constant from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 時會稽王道子以少年專政，委任群小，納望闕而歎曰：「好家居，纖兒欲撞壞之邪！

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi, still young, monopolized government and entrusted petty men; Na gazed toward the palace and sighed, saying, "What a fine household—and shall a brat be allowed to smash it!"
translations.idiomatic: While the prince of Kuaiji, Sima Daozi, was still a youth monopolizing power and filling office with small men, Lu Na looked toward the palace towers and sighed, "What a well-ordered house—and these children want to knock it flat!"

sentences.zh: 」朝士咸服其忠亮。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen all admired his loyal candor.
translations.idiomatic: Men at court respected him for that blunt loyalty.

sentences.zh: 尋除左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，未拜而卒，即以為贈。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed left grand household, bearer of the golden seal and purple ribbon; before he took office he died, and that appointment was given him posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He was named left grand household with full honors of the three excellencies but died before he could assume office; those titles were then awarded him posthumously.

sentences.zh: 長生先卒，無子。

translations.literal: Changsheng had died earlier and left no son.
translations.idiomatic: Changsheng had predeceased him without issue.

sentences.zh: 以弟子道隆嗣，元熙中，為廷尉。

translations.literal: His younger brother's son Daolong succeeded him; in the Yuanxi era he was minister of trials.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Daolong inherited the line; under the Yuanxi reign he served as minister of trials.

sentences.zh: 何充，字次道，廬江灊人，魏光祿大夫禎之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He Chong, courtesy name Cidao, was a man of Qian in Lujiang, great-grandson of Wei grand household of the palace revenues Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong, courtesy Cidao, came from Qian in Lujiang; he was the great-grandson of He Zhen, who had been Cavalier Household Grandee under Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖惲，豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun was inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He Yun had been inspector of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 父睿，安豐太守。

translations.literal: His father Rui was administrator of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: His father He Rui had governed Anfeng as prefect.

sentences.zh: 充風韻淹雅，文義見稱。

translations.literal: Chong bore refined elegance in bearing and was praised for his literary judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong combined poise with literary polish and was admired for both.

sentences.zh: 初辟大將軍王敦掾，轉主簿。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned as clerk to great general Wang Dun, then transferred to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk on Wang Dun's staff and rose to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 敦兄含時為廬江郡，貪污狼藉，敦嘗於座中稱曰：「家兄在郡定佳，廬江人士咸稱之。

translations.literal: Dun's elder brother Han at the time was in Lujiang commandery, corrupt and notorious; Dun once declared at a banquet, "My elder brother in the commandery is surely excellent; men of Lujiang all praise him."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's brother Han was then prefect of Lujiang, venal and notorious; yet at table Wang Dun boasted, "My brother's administration down there must be first-rate—the whole of Lujiang sings his praises."

sentences.zh: 」充正色曰：「充即廬江人，所聞異於此。

translations.literal: Chong with stern countenance said, "Chong is himself a man of Lujiang; what I have heard differs from this."
translations.idiomatic: He Chong answered coldly, "I am from Lujiang myself, and what I hear is not what you describe."

sentences.zh: 」敦默然。

translations.literal: Dun fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had nothing more to say.

sentences.zh: 傍人皆為之不安，充晏然自若。

translations.literal: Those beside them all felt uneasy for him, but Chong remained calm and self-possessed.
translations.idiomatic: The others squirmed for his sake, yet He Chong sat at ease.

sentences.zh: 由是忤敦，左遷東海王文學，尋屬敦敗，累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: On this account he offended Dun and was demoted to instructor for the Prince of Donghai's establishment; soon Dun was defeated, and by stages Chong was promoted to gentleman in attendance of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He earned Wang Dun's displeasure and was relegated to tutor in the prince of Donghai's household; after Wang Dun's fall he rose step by step to gentleman in attendance of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 充即王導妻之姊子，充妻，明穆皇后之妹也，故少與導善，早曆顯官。

translations.literal: Chong was the sister's son of Wang Dao's wife; Chong's wife was the younger sister of Empress Mingmu—therefore from youth he was on good terms with Dao and early held eminent office.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong was Wang Dao's nephew by marriage, and his own wife was the younger sister of Empress Mingmu, so he had been close to Wang Dao from boyhood and rose early to high rank.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣導，導以麈尾反指床呼充共坐，曰：「此是君坐也。

translations.literal: Once when visiting Dao, Dao with his fly-whisk pointed backward to the couch, calling Chong to sit with him, saying, "This is your seat."
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Wang Dao, the latter swept his fly-whisk toward the couch, beckoning He Chong to sit beside him, and said, "This place is meant for you."

sentences.zh: 」導繕揚州解會，顧而言曰：」正為次道耳。

translations.literal: Dao was repairing the headquarters office in Yangzhou; looking around he said, "It is precisely for Cidao."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao was refurbishing the Yangzhou yamen; glancing about he remarked, "The whole project is for Cidao's sake."

sentences.zh: 」明帝亦友昵之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming also treated him with friendly intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming likewise befriended him.

sentences.zh: 成帝即位，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, Chong was moved to gentleman at the yellow gates with advisory duties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng he was promoted to gentleman at the yellow gates with advisory duties.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻作亂，京都傾覆，導從駕在石頭，充東奔義軍。

translations.literal: When Su Jun raised rebellion and the capital was overturned, Dao followed the carriage at Stone Fort, while Chong fled east to the loyalist army.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun seized the capital, Wang Dao stayed with the court at Stone fortress while He Chong fled east to join the loyal forces.

sentences.zh: 其後導奔白石，充亦得還。

translations.literal: Afterward Dao fled to Baishi, and Chong also was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Dao withdrew to Baishi, and He Chong was able to rejoin him.

sentences.zh: 賊平，封都鄉侯，拜散騎常侍，出為東陽太守，仍除建威將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Chong was enfeoffed village marquis of Du, appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, went out as administrator of Dongyang, and was then given general who establishes might and interior administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Du, named cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, sent out as governor of Dongyang, then made general who establishes might and interior administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 在郡甚有德政，薦征士虞喜，拔郡人謝奉、魏顗等以為佐吏。

translations.literal: In the commandery he had very good virtuous government; he recommended the reclusive scholar Yu Xi and promoted commandery men Xie Feng and Wei Yi to serve as staff.
translations.idiomatic: His administration there was exemplary: he called up the recluse Yu Xi and appointed local men Xie Feng and Wei Yi to his staff.

sentences.zh: 後以墓被髮去郡。

translations.literal: Later because his tomb was opened he left the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later resigned the post when vandals broke into his family tombs.

sentences.zh: 詔征侍中，不拜。

translations.literal: He was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary; he declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 改葬畢，除建威將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When reburial was finished, he was appointed general who establishes might and intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the reinterment was complete he was named general who establishes might and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 王導、庾亮並言於帝曰：「何充器局方概，有萬夫之望，必能總錄朝端，為老臣之副。

translations.literal: Wang Dao and Yu Liang both spoke to the emperor, saying, "He Chong's capacity and bearing are square and grand; he has the stature to command ten thousand men and will surely be able to oversee the court as deputy to us old ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao and Yu Liang jointly told the emperor, "He Chong has the stature and backbone to lead; he can anchor the bureaucracy and stand as our junior partner in government."

sentences.zh: 臣死之日，願引充內侍，則外譽唯緝，社稷無虞矣。

translations.literal: On the day your servant dies, I wish to bring Chong in as inner attendant, then outside praise will be orderly and the altars of soil and grain will have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: When we are gone, let him serve at your side within the palace—then rumor will quiet and the altars will be safe."

sentences.zh: 」由是加吏部尚書，進號冠軍將軍，又領會稽王師。

translations.literal: On this account he was given the added post minister of personnel and advanced in title to general champion, and again concurrent tutor to the prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore added minister of personnel to his duties, raised him to general champion, and made him tutor to the prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及導薨，轉護軍將軍，與中書監庾冰參錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Dao died, Chong was transferred to general who guards the army and with Yu Bing, supervisor of the secretariat, jointly recorded overseer business for the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dao's death He Chong became general who guards the army and, with Yu Bing as supervisor of the secretariat, jointly held the recording overseer portfolio.

sentences.zh: 詔充、冰各以甲杖五十人至止車門。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chong and Bing each to bring fifty men with arms to the carriage-halt gate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed He Chong and Yu Bing each fifty armed attendants as far as the carriage-halt gate.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書令，加左將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to grand director of the secretariat with the added title general of the left.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to grand director of the secretariat with the added title general of the left.

sentences.zh: 充以內外統任，宜相糾正，若使事綜一人，於課對為嫌，乃上疏固讓。

translations.literal: Chong held that inner and outer chief duties ought to check one another; if one man monopolized affairs, it would be awkward for assessment and response; therefore he submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong argued that civil and military leadership should balance each other, and that one man holding both would skew accountability, so he memorialized repeatedly to decline the consolidation.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 徙中書令，加散騎常侍，領軍如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to supervisor of the secretariat with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; general who guards the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to supervisor of the secretariat with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary while keeping command of the guards.

sentences.zh: 又領州大中正，以州有先達宿德，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: Again concurrent senior rectifier of the province—because the province had elders of established virtue, he firmly declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was also offered senior rectifier for his province but declined firmly, citing worthier seniors already there.

sentences.zh: 庾冰兄弟以舅氏輔王室，權侔人主，慮易世之後，戚屬轉疏，將為外物所攻，謀立康帝，即帝母弟也。

translations.literal: The Yu Bing brothers, as maternal uncles assisting the royal house, wielded power equal to the ruler's; they feared that after a change of reigns their kin by marriage would grow distant and would be attacked by outsiders, and they plotted to set up Emperor Kang, who was the younger brother of the same mother as the reigning sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing and his brothers, maternal uncles steering the throne, matched the sovereign in power; they worried that after a succession their ties to the court would thin and outsiders would move against them, so they schemed to enthrone Emperor Kang, uterine brother to the sitting emperor.

sentences.zh: 每說帝以國有強敵，宜須長君，帝從之。

translations.literal: They repeatedly urged the emperor that the state faced strong enemies and needed a mature ruler; the emperor followed them.
translations.idiomatic: They kept telling the emperor that powerful foes required an adult on the throne, and he yielded.

sentences.zh: 充建議曰：「父子相傳，先王舊典，忽妄改易，懼非長計。

translations.literal: Chong submitted a proposal, saying, "Father-to-son transmission is the old norm of former kings; to alter it rashly on a whim is to be feared as no lasting plan."
translations.idiomatic: He Chong objected: "Succession from father to son is the ancient pattern; to tamper with it on a whim invites lasting harm."

sentences.zh: 故武王不授聖弟，即其義也。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wu did not hand the mandate to his sage younger brother—such is the principle.
translations.idiomatic: That is why King Wu of Zhou passed the throne to his son rather than to a worthy younger brother—it is the same principle.

sentences.zh: 昔漢景亦欲傳祚梁王，朝臣咸以為虧亂典制，據而弗聽。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Jing of Han also wished to transmit the throne to the prince of Liang; court ministers all held that it would injure and disorder the statutes and models, and relying on precedent they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jingdi once wanted to pass the throne to the prince of Liang; the whole court called it a breach of precedent and refused.

sentences.zh: 今琅邪踐阼，如孺子何！

translations.literal: Now if the prince of Langye ascends the throne, what of the child heir!"
translations.idiomatic: If the prince of Langye is set aside now, what becomes of the boy who is heir?"

sentences.zh: 社稷宗廟，將其危乎！

translations.literal: Altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temple—will they not be in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: What of the altars and the imperial shrines—will they not stand in peril?"

sentences.zh: 」冰等不從，既而康帝立，帝臨軒，冰、充侍坐。

translations.literal: Bing and the others did not follow him; afterward Emperor Kang was established; when the emperor faced the hall, Bing and Chong attended seated.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu brothers brushed him aside and enthroned Emperor Kang; at the imperial audience Yu Bing and He Chong sat in attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕嗣鴻業，二君之力也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "We inherit the great enterprise through the strength of you two lords."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I owe this great legacy to the two of you."

sentences.zh: 充對曰：「陛下龍飛，臣冰之力也。

translations.literal: Chong replied, saying, "When Your Majesty rose like a dragon, it was your servant Bing's strength."
translations.idiomatic: He Chong answered, "Your Majesty's accession was Yu Bing's doing."

sentences.zh: 若如臣議，不睹升平之世。

translations.literal: If it had been as your servant proposed, you would not have witnessed an age of rising peace."
translations.idiomatic: Had my counsel prevailed, you would not be looking on an era of peace."

sentences.zh: 」帝有慚色。

translations.literal: The emperor showed a shamefaced look.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor colored with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 建元初，出為驃騎將軍、都督徐州揚州之晉陵諸軍事、假節，領徐州刺史，鎮京口，以避諸庾。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jianyuan era he went out as general of agile cavalry, area commander for military affairs of Jinling in Xu and Yang provinces, with credential staff, concurrent inspector of Xu province, stationed at Jingkou to keep clear of the various Yus.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyuan era he was posted as general of agile cavalry and area commander over Jinling in Xu and Yang provinces, with credential staff, as inspector of Xu province at Jingkou—chiefly to escape the Yu clan's shadow.

sentences.zh: 頃之，庾翼將北伐，庾冰出鎮江州，充入朝，言於帝曰：「臣冰舅氏之重，宜居宰相，不應遠出。

translations.literal: Shortly Yu Yi was about to campaign north and Yu Bing went out to hold Jiangzhou; Chong entered court and spoke to the emperor, saying, "Your servant Bing, by weight of his maternal-uncle office, ought to hold the chancellorship and should not be sent far away."
translations.idiomatic: Soon, as Yu Yi prepared a northern expedition and Yu Bing took up post in Jiangzhou, He Chong went to court and said, "Yu Bing's stature as maternal uncle suits the chief ministership; he ought not be banished to the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」朝議不從。

translations.literal: Court deliberation did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The court majority disagreed.

sentences.zh: 於是征充入為都督揚豫徐州之琅邪諸軍事、假節，領揚州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chong was summoned in as area commander for military affairs of Langye in Yang, Yu, and Xu provinces, with credential staff, concurrent inspector of Yang province, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong was then recalled as area commander over Langye in Yang, Yu, and Xu provinces, with credential staff, and inspector of Yang province, retaining his general's commission.

sentences.zh: 先是，翼悉發江、荊二州編戶奴以充兵役，士庶嗷然。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi had conscripted every registered household slave in Jiang and Jing provinces to fill the armies; gentry and commoners clamored in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu Yi had drafted every registered bondservant in Jiang and Jing to fill the ranks, and the populace had erupted in outrage.

sentences.zh: 充復欲發揚州奴以均其謗。

translations.literal: Chong again wished to draft Yangzhou slaves to even out the blame.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong now proposed drafting Yangzhou bondservants to spread the resentment.

sentences.zh: 後以中興時已發三吳，今不宜復發而止。

translations.literal: Later because at the time of the restoration the Three Wu had already been mobilized, now it was not appropriate again to mobilize, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later, remembering that the Three Wu regions had already been tapped during the restoration, he dropped the plan as unwise to repeat.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝疾篤，冰、翼意在簡文帝，而充建議立皇太子，奏可。

translations.literal: Shortly the emperor fell gravely ill; Bing and Yi intended Emperor Jianwen, but Chong proposed establishing the heir apparent, and the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sank suddenly, Yu Bing and Yu Yi favored Prince Jianwen, but He Chong insisted on the heir apparent; his memorial carried the day.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，充奉遺旨，便立太子，是為穆帝，冰、翼甚恨之。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Chong followed the testamentary charge and at once set up the heir apparent; this was Emperor Mu; Bing and Yi deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's death He Chong carried out the will and enthroned the heir apparent—Emperor Mu—earning the bitter hatred of the Yu brothers.

sentences.zh: 獻後臨朝，詔曰：「驃騎任重，可以甲杖百人入殿。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xian held court from behind the screen; an edict said, "The general of agile cavalry bears heavy responsibility; he may enter the hall with a hundred men bearing arms."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xian assumed the regency and decreed that the general of agile cavalry, bearing such weight, might enter the hall with a hundred armed guards.

sentences.zh: 」又加中書監、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Again he was given supervisor of the secretariat and recording overseer business for the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was further named supervisor of the secretariat with the recording overseer portfolio.

sentences.zh: 充自陳既錄尚書，不宜復監中書，許之。

translations.literal: Chong personally stated that since he already recorded overseer business for the secretariat, it was not appropriate also to supervise the secretariat; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong argued that one man should not both supervise and record for the secretariat; the court agreed and split the duties.

sentences.zh: 復加侍中，羽林騎十人。

translations.literal: Again attendant-in-ordinary was added, with ten mounted guards of the feathery forest.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made attendant-in-ordinary with ten mounted guards from the feathery forest.

sentences.zh: 冰、翼等尋卒，充專輔幼主。

translations.literal: Bing, Yi, and the others soon died; Chong alone assisted the young sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Bing and Yu Yi died in quick succession, He Chong became the sole pillar of the boy emperor.

sentences.zh: 翼臨終，表以後任委息爰之。

translations.literal: On his deathbed Yi memorialized that his successor duty be entrusted to his son Yuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi's deathbed memorial asked that his son Yuanzhi inherit his western command.

sentences.zh: 于時論者並以諸庾世在西籓，人情所歸，宜依翼所請，以安物情。

translations.literal: At the time debaters all held that for generations the Yus had guarded the western marches and commanded men's hearts; they ought to follow Yi's request to settle sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion then held that the Yu clan had long held the western defense and enjoyed the army's trust, and that honoring Yu Yi's wish would steady the mood of the realm.

sentences.zh: 充曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Chong said, "It is not so."
translations.idiomatic: He Chong said, "That will not do."

sentences.zh: 荊楚國之西門，戶口百萬，北帶強胡，西鄰勁蜀，經略險阻，周旋萬里。

translations.literal: Jing-Chu is the western gate of the state, with a million registered households, strong Hu pressed against the north, and hardy Shu bordering the west; its terrain is perilous and its circuits run ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou is the empire's western gate: a million households, powerful steppe peoples to the north, tough Shu to the west, and rugged country stretching for thousands of miles.

sentences.zh: 得賢則中原可定，勢弱則社稷同憂，所謂陸抗存則吳存，抗亡則吳亡者，豈可以白麵年少猥當此任哉！

translations.literal: If one obtains a worthy man the Central Plain can be settled; if the power is weak then the altars share the worry—what they called "while Lu Kang lived Wu lived, when Kang died Wu died"—how can a pale-faced youth be lightly given this charge!"
translations.idiomatic: A capable commander secures the heartland; a weak one puts the dynasty itself at risk—as they said of Wu, "While Lu Kang lived, Wu lived; when he died, Wu perished." How can we hand that burden to a boy with a scholar's complexion?"

sentences.zh: 桓溫英略過人，有文武識度，西夏之任，無出溫者。

translations.literal: Huan Wen surpasses others in heroic design and has civil and military insight and measure; for the western Xia post none surpasses Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's strategic gifts outstrip others', and he combines civil insight with military nerve; for the western command no one matches him."

sentences.zh: 」議者又曰：「庾爰之肯避溫乎？

translations.literal: Discussants again said, "Will Yu Yuanzhi be willing to yield to Wen?"
translations.idiomatic: Critics objected, "Will Yu Yuanzhi step aside for Huan Wen?"

sentences.zh: 如令阻兵，恥懼不淺。

translations.literal: If he should block the army, shame and fear would not be shallow.
translations.idiomatic: If he defies the transfer with troops, the humiliation and danger would be grave.

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「溫足能制之，諸君勿憂。

translations.literal: Chong said, "Wen is fully able to control him; gentlemen, do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: He Chong replied, "Huan Wen can handle him; you need not fear."

sentences.zh: 」乃使溫西。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Wen west.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent Huan Wen west in Yu Yi's place.

sentences.zh: 爰之果不敢爭。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi indeed did not dare contend.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuanzhi dared not resist.

sentences.zh: 充以衛將軍褚裒皇太后父，宜綜朝政，上疏薦裒參錄尚書。

translations.literal: Chong held that General Who Guards the Guard Chu Pou, the empress dowager's father, ought to oversee court government; he submitted a memorial recommending Pou jointly record overseer business for the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because General Who Guards the Guard Chu Pou was the empress dowager's father, He Chong thought he should share in steering the government and recommended him for joint recording overseer duties.

sentences.zh: 裒以地逼，固求外出。

translations.literal: Pou because proximity to the throne was pressing firmly requested to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou, feeling the awkwardness of kinship too close to the throne, begged for a provincial posting instead.

sentences.zh: 充每曰：「桓溫、褚裒為方伯，殷浩居門下，我可無勞矣。」

translations.literal: Chong often said, "With Huan Wen and Chu Pou as regional commanders and Yin Hao at the gate department, I can be without labor."
translations.idiomatic: He Chong used to say, "With Huan Wen and Chu Pou holding the provinces and Yin Hao minding the gate bureau, I may be spared the heavy lifting myself."

sentences.zh: 充居宰相，雖無澄正改革之能，而強力有器局，臨朝正色，以社稷為己任，凡所選用，皆以功臣為先，不以私恩樹親戚，談者以此重之。

translations.literal: Though Chong held the chancellorship, though he lacked the ability to clarify and rectify or carry out reform, he was forceful and had capacity and bearing; facing court with stern mien he took the altars as his own charge; in all appointments he put merit ministers first and did not plant kin through private favor—discussants for this reason respected him.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister He Chong never mastered sweeping reform, but he was strong-willed and broad-shouldered; he kept a grave face at audience and treated the altars as his personal charge. He always promoted men of proven service before kin, and opinion respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 然所昵庸雜，信任不得其人，而性好釋典，崇修佛寺，供給沙門以百數，糜費巨億而不吝也。

translations.literal: Yet those he favored were mediocre and mixed, and those he trusted were not the right men; moreover his nature loved Buddhist sutras and he exalted and repaired Buddhist temples, supplying śramaṇas numbering over a hundred, squandering sums in the hundreds of millions without stint.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he surrounded himself with mediocrities and misplaced trust, doted on Buddhist scripture, poured silver into temple-building, and maintained well over a hundred monks at court expense without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 親友至於貧乏，無所施遺，以此獲譏於世。

translations.literal: As to kin and friends who fell into want, he had nothing to give them; for this he incurred ridicule in the world.
translations.idiomatic: When kinsmen and friends fell on hard times he offered no relief, and the world mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 阮裕嘗戲之曰：「卿志大宇宙，勇邁終古。

translations.literal: Ruan Yu once teased him, saying, "Your ambition is as vast as the cosmos; your courage surpasses all ages."
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yu once teased He Chong: "You aim as high as heaven and earth; you fancy yourself bolder than anyone who ever lived."

sentences.zh: 」充問其故。

translations.literal: Chong asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong asked what he meant.

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「我圖數千戶郡尚未能得，卿圖作佛，不亦大乎！

translations.literal: Yu said, "I have not yet been able to obtain a commandery of several thousand households, yet you scheme to become a Buddha—is it not grand!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yu answered, "I cannot even win a middling prefecture, while you set your heart on becoming a Buddha—that is ambition on another scale altogether!"

sentences.zh: 」于時郗愔及弟曇奉天師道，而充與弟崇准信釋氏，謝萬譏之云：「二郗諂於道，二何佞於佛。

translations.literal: At the time Xi Yin and his younger brother Tan followed the Celestial Master Way, while He Chong and his younger brother He Cong were devoted to the Śākya clan; Xie Wan ridiculed them, saying, "The two Xis flatter the Way; the two Hes flatter the Buddha."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin and his brother Tan followed the Celestial Master sect, while He Chong and his brother He Cong placed their faith in Buddhism; Xie Wan mocked them as "the two Xis toadying to the Dao and the two Hes toadying to the Buddha."

sentences.zh: 」充能飲酒，雅為劉惔所貴。

translations.literal: Chong could drink wine and was highly prized by Liu Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong was a capable drinker whom Liu Tan prized above others.

sentences.zh: 惔每云：「見次道飲，令人欲傾家釀。

translations.literal: Tan would always say, "Watching Cidao drink makes one want to pour out the whole household brew."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan used to say, "Watching Cidao hold his liquor makes you want to broach every jar in the house."

sentences.zh: 」言其能溫克也。

translations.literal: It means that he could drink in moderation and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that He Chong could drink deeply yet stay steady.

sentences.zh: 永和二年卒，時年五十五，贈司空，諡曰文穆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghe (346) he died at age fifty-five; posthumously he was awarded minister of works with the posthumous name Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 346 at fifty-five, posthumously honored as minister of works with the epithet Wenmu, "Accomplished and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 無子，弟子放嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother's son Fang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, so his nephew Fang inherited his line.

sentences.zh: 卒，又無子，又以兄孫松嗣，位至驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Fang died, again there was no son, and his elder brother's grandson Song succeeded him, rising to staff adviser to the general of agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang in turn died without issue, the grandson Song inherited; Song rose to advising secretary on the staff of the general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 充弟准，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Zhun is treated in the "Treatise on Outer Kin."
translations.idiomatic: His brother He Zhun has a separate biography under the outer kin.

sentences.zh: 褚翜，字謀遠，太傅裒之從父兄也。

translations.literal: Chu Se, courtesy name Mouyuan, was the elder patriline cousin once removed of Grand Tutor Pou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Se, courtesy Mouyuan, was a first cousin once removed of Grand Tutor Chu Pou.

sentences.zh: 父頠，少知名，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Wei was known from youth and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chu Wei won a name while young but died young.

sentences.zh: 翜以才藝楨幹稱。

translations.literal: Se was praised for talent, arts, and backbone fit for state timber.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Se was esteemed for talent, polish, and the backbone needed in high office.

sentences.zh: 襲爵關內侯，補冠軍參軍。

translations.literal: He inherited the noble rank marquis within the passes and was appointed adjutant to the champion general.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the rank of marquis within the passes and became an adjutant on the champion general's staff.

sentences.zh: 于時長沙王乂擅權，成都、河間阻兵於外，翜知內難方作，乃棄官避地幽州。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Changsha Yi monopolized power, while Chengdu and Hejian blocked the army outside; Se knew internal disaster was about to arise, so he resigned office and fled to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima Yi of Changsha seized power and the princes of Chengdu and Hejian held armies in the field, Chu Se saw civil war coming and quit his post to take refuge in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 後河北有寇難，復還鄉里。

translations.literal: Later there was bandit trouble north of the Yellow River, and he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Raids later drove him from the north, and he went home again.

sentences.zh: 河南尹舉翜行本縣事。

translations.literal: The intendant of Henan nominated Se to act in the affairs of his home county.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan intendant appointed him acting magistrate of his native county.

sentences.zh: 及天下鼎沸，翜招合同志，將圖過江，先移住陽城界。

translations.literal: When the realm boiled over, Se gathered like-minded men and planned to cross the Yangzi, first moving to lodge within the borders of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire collapsed he rallied allies intent on crossing south and camped first in Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 潁川庾敳，即翜之舅也，亦憂世亂，以家付翜。

translations.literal: Yingchuan Yu Kai, who was Se's maternal uncle, also worried at the age's turmoil and entrusted his household to Se.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yu Kai of Yingchuan, equally alarmed by the chaos, handed his family into Chu Se's care.

sentences.zh: 翜道斷，不得前。

translations.literal: The roads were cut off and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting blocked the roads and he could not get through.

sentences.zh: 東海王越以為參軍，辭疾不就。

translations.literal: Prince of Donghai Yue appointed him adjutant, but he declined on grounds of illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, prince of Donghai, named him adjutant, but he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 尋洛陽覆沒，與滎陽太守郭秀共保萬氏台，秀不能綏眾，與將陳撫、郭重等構怨，遂相攻擊。

translations.literal: Soon Luoyang fell; together with Administrator of Xingyang Guo Xiu he held Wan's Terrace, but Xiu could not pacify the host and with commanders Chen Fu, Guo Zhong, and others nursed grudges until they turned on one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he joined Xingyang prefect Guo Xiu in defending Wan's Terrace; Guo Xiu failed to keep order, and his officers Chen Fu and Guo Zhong fell to feuding until they attacked one another.

sentences.zh: 翜懼禍及，謂撫等曰：「以諸君所以在此，謀逃難也。

translations.literal: Se feared disaster would reach him and said to Fu and the others, "The reason you gentlemen are here is to plot escape from calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the violence would engulf him, Chu Se told Chen Fu and the rest, "You came here to flee disaster, not to court it."

sentences.zh: 今宜共戮力以備賊，幸無外難，而內自相擊，是避坑落井也。

translations.literal: Now you ought together to exert strength to prepare against bandits; fortunately there is no trouble from without, yet within you strike one another—it is to flee a pit and fall into a well.
translations.idiomatic: You should combine your strength against the enemy. With no foe at the gates you are tearing each other apart—leaping out of a ditch only to drop into a well."

sentences.zh: 郭秀誠為失理，應且容之。

translations.literal: Guo Xiu is indeed in the wrong, but you ought for the moment to tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiu may be unreasonable, but forbearance is the wiser course now."

sentences.zh: 若遂所忿，城內自潰，胡賊聞之，指來掩襲，諸君雖得殺秀，無解胡虜矣，累弱非一，宜深思之。

translations.literal: If you follow your resentments to the end, the city will collapse from within; when the Hu raiders hear of it they will come in a sudden strike—though you may kill Guo Xiu, you will not save yourselves from the Hu; the harm to wives and children will not be one fold only—think deeply on it."
translations.idiomatic: If you indulge this feud the garrison will destroy itself from within; the moment barbarian raiders hear of it they will swoop in. Killing Guo Xiu will not save you from them, and the women and children will suffer beyond measure—think again."

sentences.zh: 」撫等悔悟，與秀交和。

translations.literal: Fu and the others repented and made peace with Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fu and his comrades relented and made peace with Guo Xiu.

sentences.zh: 時數萬口賴翜獲全。

translations.literal: At the time several tens of thousands of lives depended on Se and were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of refugees owed their survival to Chu Se.

sentences.zh: 明年，率數千家將謀東下，遇道險，不得進，因留密縣。

translations.literal: The next year he led several thousand households planning to go east but met blocked roads and could not advance, and therefore stayed at Mi county.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he shepherded several thousand families eastward but found the roads impassable and halted at Mi county.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉荀組以為參軍、廣威將軍，復領本縣，率邑人三千，督新城、梁、陽城三郡諸營事。

translations.literal: Metropolitan commandant Xun Zu appointed him adjutant and general who spreads might, again to head his home county, leading three thousand townsmen to oversee camp affairs in the three commanderies Xincheng, Liang, and Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Xun Zu made him adjutant and general who spreads might, again put him in charge of his home county, and assigned him three thousand local militiamen to coordinate the camps of Xincheng, Liang, and Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷司隸司馬，仍督營事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was moved to metropolitan marshal of the province while still overseeing camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became provincial metropolitan marshal while continuing to direct the camps.

sentences.zh: 率眾進至汝水柴肥口，復阻賊。

translations.literal: He led the host forward to the Chifei ford on the Ru River and again was blocked by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to the Chifei crossing on the Ru River and again ran into rebel forces.
