sentences.zh: 翜乃單馬至許昌，見司空荀籓，以為振威將軍，行梁國內史。

translations.literal: Se then rode alone to Xuchang, saw Minister of Works Xun Fan, and was appointed general who rouses might, acting interior administrator of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Se rode alone to Xuchang, saw Minister of Works Xun Fan, and was named general who rouses might with acting authority as interior administrator of Liang.

sentences.zh: 建興初，復為豫州司馬，督司州軍事。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jianxing era he again became metropolitan marshal of Yu province, overseeing military affairs of Si province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianxing he was again made metropolitan marshal of Yu province with charge of Si province's armies.

sentences.zh: 太傅參軍王玄代翜為郡。

translations.literal: Adjutant to the grand tutor Wang Xuan replaced Se in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor staff officer Wang Xuan succeeded Chu Se as prefect of Liang.

sentences.zh: 時梁國部曲將耿奴甚得人情，而專勢，翜常優遇之。

translations.literal: At the time Geng Nu, a household-troop commander of Liang commandery, was very popular with the men but monopolized power; Se always treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nu, a retainer captain in Liang, was beloved by the troops yet overbearing; Chu Se treated him with consistent generosity.

sentences.zh: 玄為政既急，翜知其不能容奴，因戒之曰：「卿威殺已多，而人情難一，宜深慎之。

translations.literal: Xuan's administration was harsh; Se knew he could not tolerate Nu, and therefore warned him, saying, "You have already killed many by intimidation, yet men's hearts are hard to unify—you ought to be deeply cautious."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan governed with a heavy hand; Chu Se knew he would not tolerate Geng Nu and warned him, "You have already shed much blood; winning hearts is harder than breaking them—tread carefully."

sentences.zh: 」玄納翜言，外羈縻奴，而內懷憤。

translations.literal: Xuan accepted Se's words outwardly kept Nu on a loose rein while inwardly harboring resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan took the advice, outwardly indulging Geng Nu while nursing a grudge.

sentences.zh: 會遷為陳留，將發，乃收奴斬之。

translations.literal: When he was about to be transferred to Chenliu and set to depart, he then seized Nu and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his transfer to Chenliu he arrested Geng Nu and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 翜奴餘黨聚眾殺玄。

translations.literal: The remnant faction of Nu's followers gathered a mob and killed Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nu's diehards rallied, stormed his yamen, and killed Wang Xuan.

sentences.zh: 梁郡既有內難，而徐州賊張平等欲掩襲之。

translations.literal: Liang commandery already had internal disaster, while bandits of Xu province such as Zhang Ping wished to raid it.
translations.idiomatic: With Liang in turmoil, Xu bandits led by Zhang Ping prepared to strike.

sentences.zh: 郡人遑惑，將以郡歸平。

translations.literal: The people of the commandery were panicked and were about to hand the commandery over to Ping.
translations.idiomatic: The terrified populace was ready to surrender the prefecture to Zhang Ping.

sentences.zh: 荀組遣翜往撫之，眾心乃定。

translations.literal: Xun Zu sent Se to pacify them, and the hearts of the host were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu dispatched Chu Se to calm them, and order returned.

sentences.zh: 頃之，組舉翜為吏部郎，不應召，遂東過江。

translations.literal: Shortly Zu nominated Se as gentleman in the ministry of personnel; he did not answer the summons and crossed the Yangzi eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu soon recommended him for the ministry of personnel, but Chu Se ignored the call and crossed the river south.

sentences.zh: 元帝為晉王，以翜為散騎郎，轉太子中庶子，出為奮威將軍、淮南內史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was prince of Jin, he appointed Se cavalier gentleman in attendance, transferred him to junior tutor to the heir apparent, sent him out as general who exerts martial might and interior administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: As prince of Jin, Sima Rui named Chu Se cavalier gentleman in attendance, then junior tutor to the heir apparent, then general who exerts martial might and interior administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，王敦構逆，征西將軍戴若思令翜出軍赴難，翜遣將領五百人從之。

translations.literal: At the start of the Yongchang era Wang Dun plotted rebellion; General Who Guards the West Dai Ruosi ordered Se to dispatch troops to relieve the capital, and Se sent a commander with five hundred men to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongchang, when Wang Dun rebelled, Dai Ruosi ordered Chu Se to send relief; Chu Se detached five hundred men under a commander.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，徵拜屯騎校尉，遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Se was summoned as colonel of the camp garrison, then moved to left commandant who guards the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he became colonel of the camp garrison, then left commandant guarding the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 成帝初，為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Cheng's reign he was general of the left guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng came to the throne he served as general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之役，朝廷戒嚴，以翜為侍中，典征討軍事。

translations.literal: During the Su Jun campaign the court was on full alert and appointed Se attendant-in-ordinary, in charge of military affairs for the punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's revolt the court declared martial law and named Chu Se attendant-in-ordinary to direct the war effort.

sentences.zh: 既而王師敗績，司徒王導謂翜曰：「至尊當禦正殿，君可啟令速出。

translations.literal: Afterward the royal army was defeated; Minister of Education Wang Dao said to Se, "The sovereign ought to take his seat in the main hall; you may enter and urge him to come out quickly."
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial army collapsed, Wang Dao told Chu Se, "The emperor must appear in the main hall; go in at once and bring him out."

sentences.zh: 」翜即入上大閣，躬自抱帝登太極前殿。

translations.literal: Se then entered the great upper gallery, personally embraced the emperor, and ascended to the Taiji front hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Se entered the upper gallery, lifted the boy emperor in his arms, and carried him to the Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 導升御床抱帝，翜及鐘雅、劉超侍立左右。

translations.literal: Dao ascended the imperial couch and embraced the emperor; Se together with Zhong Ya and Liu Chao stood attending to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao mounted the dais and held the emperor while Chu Se, Zhong Ya, and Liu Chao flanked them.

sentences.zh: 時百官奔散，殿省蕭然。

translations.literal: At the time the hundred officials had fled in disorder; the halls and secretariat were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: The officials had scattered; the palace corridors stood empty.

sentences.zh: 峻兵既入，叱翜令下。

translations.literal: When Jun's troops had entered, they shouted at Se to come down.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's men barked at Chu Se to step down from the dais.

sentences.zh: 翜正立不動，呵之曰：「蘇冠軍來覲至尊，軍人豈得侵逼！

translations.literal: Se stood straight without moving and rebuked them, saying, "General Su the champion comes to pay court to the sovereign—how dare soldiers press in!"
translations.idiomatic: Chu Se stood rigid and shouted back, "General Su comes as a champion to greet the Son of Heaven—soldiers have no business threatening him!"

sentences.zh: 」由是兵士不敢上殿。

translations.literal: On this account the troops did not dare ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The awed troops dared not mount the steps.

sentences.zh: 及峻執政，猶以為侍中，從乘輿幸石頭。

translations.literal: When Jun held power he still kept Se as attendant-in-ordinary and followed the imperial carriage to Stone Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Even under Su Jun's dictatorship Chu Se remained attendant-in-ordinary and accompanied the court to Stone fortress.

sentences.zh: 明年，與光祿大夫陸曄等出據苑城。

translations.literal: The next year together with Grand Household of the Palace Revenues Lu Ye and others he went out to hold Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined Lu Ye and others in occupying Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 蘇逸、任讓圍之，翜等固守。

translations.literal: Su Yi and Ren Rang besieged them; Se and the others held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yi and Ren Rang besieged the loyalists, who held their ground.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功封長平縣伯，遷丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, for merit he was enfeoffed village baron of Changping and moved to intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fell he was enfeoffed as village baron of Changping for his service and promoted intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時京邑焚蕩，人物凋殘，翜收集散亡，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: At the time the capital had been burned and laid waste and persons were withered; Se gathered the scattered and lost and had very benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was in ashes and the population decimated; Chu Se gathered refugees and governed with conspicuous kindness.

sentences.zh: 代庾亮為中護軍，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: He replaced Yu Liang as general who guards the army, stationed at Stone Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Yu Liang as general who guards the army, holding Stone fortress.

sentences.zh: 尋為領軍，徙五兵尚書，加奉車都尉，監新宮事。

translations.literal: Soon he was commanding general, moved to minister of the five military divisions, with the added title colonel who follows the carriage, supervising construction of the new palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he headed the guards, became minister of the five divisions, added colonel who follows the carriage, and oversaw the new palace works.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射，轉左僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was moved to right vice director of the secretariat, transferred to left vice director, with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice director of the secretariat, then left vice director, with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary added.

sentences.zh: 久之，代何充為護軍將軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: After a long time he replaced He Chong as general who guards the army; attendant-in-ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he replaced He Chong as commanding general of the guards while keeping his cavalier attendant post.

sentences.zh: 咸康七年卒，時年六十七，贈衛將軍，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang (341) he died at age sixty-seven; posthumously he was awarded general who guards the guard with the posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 341 at sixty-seven, posthumously honored as general who guards the guard with the epithet Mu.

sentences.zh: 子希嗣，官至豫章太守。

translations.literal: His son Xi succeeded him; his office reached administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chu Xi inherited the title and rose to governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 蔡謨，字道明，陳留考城人也。

translations.literal: Cai Mo, courtesy name Daoming, was a man of Kaocheng in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo, courtesy Daoming, came from Kaocheng in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 世為著姓。

translations.literal: For generations they were a noted surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Cais had been a leading clan for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖睦，魏尚書。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Mu was minister of the secretariat under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Cai Mu had been a Wei minister of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖德，樂平太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather De was administrator of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cai De governed Leping as prefect.

sentences.zh: 父克，少好學，博涉書記，為邦族所敬。

translations.literal: His father Ke from youth loved learning, broadly perused documents and records, and was revered by the commandery clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cai Ke loved books from boyhood, read widely, and commanded the respect of the local gentry.

sentences.zh: 性公亮守正，行不合己，雖富貴不交也。

translations.literal: By nature he was fair, bright, and upheld the right; if conduct did not match his own standards, even the rich and noble he would not associate with.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and principled: he would not befriend anyone, however grand, whose conduct failed his standard.

sentences.zh: 高平劉整恃才縱誕，服飾詭異，無所拘忌。

translations.literal: Liu Zheng of Gaoping, relying on talent, gave free rein to eccentricity; dress and adornment were bizarre and he observed no restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng of Gaoping, confident in his wit, flaunted outlandish dress and wild manners without restraint.

sentences.zh: 嘗行造人，遇克在坐，整終席慚不自安。

translations.literal: Once when traveling to visit someone he encountered Ke seated among the company; for the whole sitting Zheng was ashamed and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Once, calling on friends, he found Cai Ke among the guests and squirmed in embarrassment the entire evening.

sentences.zh: 克時為處士，而見憚如此。

translations.literal: At the time Ke was a recluse without office, yet he was feared to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ke was still a private scholar, yet he could intimidate such a man.

sentences.zh: 後為成都王穎大將軍記室督。

translations.literal: Later he became recorder-in-chief on the staff of great general Prince of Chengdu Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Prince Sima Ying of Chengdu as recorder-in-chief on the great general's staff.

sentences.zh: 穎為丞相，擢為東曹掾。

translations.literal: When Ying was chancellor, Ke was promoted clerk of the eastern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying became chancellor he promoted Cai Ke to the eastern bureau.

sentences.zh: 克素有格量，及居選官，苟進之徒，望風畏憚。

translations.literal: Ke from of old had capacity and measure; when he held the post of selector, those who advanced through improper routes feared him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ke had always shown judgment; as personnel selector he made careerists shrink at a distance.

sentences.zh: 初，克未仕時，河內山簡嘗與琅邪王衍書曰：「蔡子尼今之正人。

translations.literal: At first, before Ke had taken office, Shan Jian of Henei once wrote to Wang Yan of Langye, saying, "Cai Zini is the upright man of today."
translations.idiomatic: Before Cai Ke ever served, Shan Jian of Henei wrote Wang Yan of Langye calling Cai Zini the most upright man of the age.

sentences.zh: 」衍以書示眾曰：「山子以一字拔人，然未易可稱。

translations.literal: Yan showed the letter to the assembly, saying, "Shanzi with one character elevates a man, yet it is not easy to deserve the praise."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan read the letter aloud and said, "Shan Jian praises a man in a single phrase, but living up to it is another matter."

sentences.zh: 」後衍聞克在選官，曰：「山子正人之言，驗於今矣。

translations.literal: Later when Yan heard that Ke held the selector's office, he said, "Shanzi's words about an upright man are verified today."
translations.idiomatic: Later, learning that Cai Ke held the selector's post, Wang Yan said, "Shan Jian's judgment stands vindicated."

sentences.zh: 」陳留時為大郡，號稱多士，琅邪王澄行經其界，太守呂豫遣吏迎之。

translations.literal: Chenliu at the time was a great commandery famed for hosting many gentlemen; Wang Cheng of Langye passed through its borders, and Administrator Lü Yu sent clerks to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu was then a major prefecture crowded with talent. Wang Cheng of Langye passed through its territory, and Prefect Lü Yu sent clerks to greet him.

sentences.zh: 澄人境問吏曰：「此郡人士為誰？

translations.literal: When Cheng entered the borders he asked the clerk, "Who in this commandery counts as a gentleman of note?"
translations.idiomatic: At the border Wang Cheng asked, "Whom does this commandery reckon among its leading men?"

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「有蔡子尼、江應元。

translations.literal: The clerk said, "There are Cai Zini and Jiang Yingyuan."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk answered, "Cai Zini and Jiang Yingyuan."

sentences.zh: 」是時郡人多居大位者，澄以其姓名問曰：「甲乙等，非君郡人邪？

translations.literal: At the time many men of the commandery already held high position; Cheng asked their names, saying, "Are not persons A and B men of your commandery?"
translations.idiomatic: Many locals already held high rank, so Wang Cheng rattled off several names: "Surely these men are from your commandery too?"

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「是也。

translations.literal: The clerk said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk said they were.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「然則何以但稱此二人？

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Then why did you name only these two?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng asked why only the first pair had been mentioned.

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「向謂君侯問人，不謂問位。

translations.literal: The clerk said, "I thought my lord was asking about men, not about offices."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk replied, "I thought you asked for men of quality, not for rank."

sentences.zh: 」澄笑而止。

translations.literal: Cheng laughed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng laughed and dropped the subject.

sentences.zh: 到郡，以吏言謂豫曰：「舊名此郡有風俗，果然小吏亦知如此。

translations.literal: When he reached the commandery he told Yu what the clerk had said: "By old repute this commandery has a distinctive ethos; truly even a petty clerk knows thus."
translations.idiomatic: At the yamen he repeated the exchange to Lü Yu: "They say this prefecture has character; even a lowly clerk proves it."

sentences.zh: 」克以朝政日弊，遂絕不仕。

translations.literal: Ke because court government daily worsened resolved never to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Watching court politics rot, Cai Ke resolved never to serve.

sentences.zh: 東嬴公騰為車騎將軍，鎮河北，以克為從事中郎，知必不就，以軍期致之。

translations.literal: Duke of Dongying Teng was general who commands chariots and cavalry, holding the north of the Yellow River, and appointed Ke retainer clerk; knowing Ke would surely not come, he summoned him with a military deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng, duke of Dongying, was general of chariots and cavalry on the northern frontier and named Cai Ke retainer clerk; knowing he would refuse, Sima Teng used a military summons to force him.

sentences.zh: 克不得已，至數十日，騰為汲桑所攻，城陷，克見害。

translations.literal: Ke having no choice, after several tens of days Teng was attacked by Ji Sang and the city fell; Ke was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ke yielded at last but within weeks Ji Sang stormed Sima Teng's city; Cai Ke died in the sack.

sentences.zh: 謨弱冠察孝廉，州辟從事，舉秀才，東海王越召為掾，皆不就。

translations.literal: Mo at the weak-capped years was examined filially incorrupt, summoned by the province as retainer clerk, nominated flourishing talent, summoned by Prince of Donghai Yue as clerk—all of which he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo, capped at twenty, was recommended filially incorrupt, called to provincial staff, nominated flourishing talent, and invited by Sima Yue—he refused every offer.

sentences.zh: 避亂渡江。

translations.literal: He fled turmoil and crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi to escape the wars.

sentences.zh: 時明帝為東中郎將，引為參軍。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Ming was general who guards the east and brought him in as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, then general who guards the east, took him on as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 元帝拜丞相，復辟為掾，轉參軍，後為中書侍郎，曆義興太守、大將軍王敦從事中郎、司徒左長史，遷侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was appointed chancellor he again summoned him as clerk, transferred him to adjutant, later to gentleman in attendance of the secretariat, passing through administrator of Yixing, retainer clerk to great general Wang Dun, chief clerk to the minister of education, left chief clerk, and promotion to attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui became chancellor he recalled Cai Mo as clerk, moved him to adjutant, then gentleman in attendance of the secretariat, then through governor of Yixing, retainer to Wang Dun, chief clerk under the minister of education, left chief clerk, and finally attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻構逆，吳國內史庾冰出奔會稽，乃以謨為吳國內史。

translations.literal: When Su Jun plotted rebellion, interior administrator of Wu Yu Bing fled to Kuaiji, and Mo was therefore appointed interior administrator of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rose, Yu Bing fled the Wu interior command to Kuaiji, and Cai Mo was named interior administrator of Wu in his place.

sentences.zh: 謨既至，與張闓、顧眾、顧颺等共起義兵，迎冰還郡。

translations.literal: When Mo had arrived, together with Zhang Kai, Gu Zhong, Gu Yang, and others he jointly raised loyalist troops and welcomed Bing back to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After landing in Wu, Cai Mo joined Zhang Kai, Gu Zhong, Gu Yang, and others in raising loyal militia that escorted Yu Bing back to his seat.

sentences.zh: 峻平，復為侍中，遷五兵尚書，領琅邪王師。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified, Mo again became attendant-in-ordinary, was moved to minister of the five military divisions, concurrent tutor to the prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Once Su Jun fell, Cai Mo regained his post as attendant-in-ordinary, became minister of the five divisions, and resumed his role as tutor to the prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 謨上疏讓曰：「八坐之任，非賢莫居，前後所用，資名有常。

translations.literal: Mo submitted a memorial declining, saying, "The posts of the eight seats are such that none but worthies occupy them; those employed before and after have stable qualification and reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo memorialized his refusal: "The Eight Seats belong only to men of proven merit; previous appointments followed clear rules of seniority and name."

sentences.zh: 孔愉、諸葛恢並以清節令才，少著名望。

translations.literal: Kong Yu and Zhuge Hui alike by pure conduct and admirable talent in youth had already established fame.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu and Zhuge Hui had both earned reputations early for integrity and talent.

sentences.zh: 昔愉為御史中丞，臣尚為司徒長史；

translations.literal: Formerly when Yu was imperial censor, your servant was still chief clerk to the minister of education;
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Yu was censor-in-chief, I was only chief clerk under the minister of education;

sentences.zh: 恢為會稽太守，臣為尚書郎；

translations.literal: when Hui was interior administrator of Kuaiji, your servant was a gentleman in the secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: when Zhuge Hui governed Kuaiji, I held a low secretariat post;

sentences.zh: 恢尹丹陽，臣守小郡。

translations.literal: when Hui intendanted Danyang, your servant guarded a small commandery.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhuge Hui ran Danyang, I commanded a minor county.

sentences.zh: 名輩不同，階級殊懸。

translations.literal: Their generations and ranks were not the same; the steps between us were vastly distant.
translations.idiomatic: Our standing and our ranks were worlds apart.

sentences.zh: 今猥以輕鄙，超倫逾等，上亂聖朝貫魚之序，下違群士准平之論。

translations.literal: Now meanly with my light vulgarity I leap past classes and overstep ranks, above disturbing the sagely court's proper ordering like a string of fish, below violating the gentlemen's standard of fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Now a mediocrity like me would vault over heads, disordering the throne's careful ranking and flouting every fair judgment below.

sentences.zh: 豈惟微臣其亡之誡，實招聖政惟塵之累。

translations.literal: Is it only your servant's lesson of ruin that is summoned—truly it invites the stain of sagely governance gathering dust.
translations.idiomatic: It invites not merely my downfall but the smear of a policy grown dusty from neglect.

sentences.zh: 且左長史一超而侍帷幄，再登而廁納言，中興已來，上德之舉所未嘗有。

translations.literal: Moreover the left chief clerk in one leap attends within the curtain hangings, in a second ascension sits among the spokesmen—since the restoration such elevation of superior virtue has never occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Never since the restoration has a left chief clerk leaped twice in succession from the inner chamber to the rank of chief spokesman—nothing like it has honored "superior virtue."

sentences.zh: 臣何人斯，而猥當之！

translations.literal: What manner of man is your servant, that meanly he should bear this!
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man am I to deserve such leaps?

sentences.zh: 是以叩心自忖，三省愚身，與其苟進以穢清塗，寧受違命狷固之罪。

translations.literal: Therefore knocking the heart and examining himself, thrice examining his foolish person, rather than recklessly advancing to defile a pure path, he would rather bear the crime of refusing orders out of stubbornness.
translations.idiomatic: I have searched my conscience: better the crime of mulish disobedience than scrambling forward to foul a pure track."

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，不許。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused his plea.

sentences.zh: 轉掌吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to hold the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was rotated into control of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 以平蘇峻勳，賜爵濟陽男，又讓，不許。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Su Jun he was granted the noble rank male of Jiyang; again he declined; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the viscounty of Jiyang for defeating Su Jun, declined it again, and was again overruled.

sentences.zh: 冬蒸，謨領祠部，主者忘設明帝位，與太常張泉俱免，白衣領職。

translations.literal: At the winter steam-offering Mo headed the department of sacrifices; the responsible official forgot to set out Emperor Ming's seat; together with grand astrologer Zhang Quan he was dismissed, serving in white garments while holding office.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter sacrifice Cai Mo supervised the ritual office; the registrar omitted Emperor Ming's tablet, so he was cashiered along with Grand Astrologer Zhang Quan and resumed duty in undyed robes pending review.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷太常，領秘書監，以疾不堪親職，上疏自解，不聽。

translations.literal: Shortly he was moved to grand astrologer, concurrent supervisor of the library; because of illness he could not attend duties in person and submitted a memorial resigning; he was not permitted to listen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named grand astrologer and librarian, pleaded illness, asked to resign, and was refused.

sentences.zh: 成帝臨軒，遣使拜太傅、太尉、司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng faced the hall he dispatched envoys to invest grand tutor, grand commandant, and minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng held court and sent envoys to invest the grand tutor, grand commandant, and minister of works.

sentences.zh: 會將作樂，宿縣於殿庭，門下奏，非祭祀燕饗則無設樂之制。

translations.literal: Music was to be performed and chimes were hung overnight in the courtyard; the gate department memorialized that apart from sacrifice or banquet feasting there was no institution for setting up music.
translations.idiomatic: Court musicians were to hang bells in the courtyard overnight; the gate bureau objected that only sacrifice or state feast justified music there.

sentences.zh: 事下太常。

translations.literal: The matter was handed to the grand astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: The question went to the ritual office.

sentences.zh: 謨議臨軒遣使宜有金石之樂，遂從之。

translations.literal: Mo held that when facing the hall and dispatching envoys there ought to be metal and stone music; thereupon they followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo argued that an investiture audience required bronze and stone music, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 臨軒作樂，自此始也。

translations.literal: Facing the hall with music began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began the practice of playing ritual music at such audiences.

sentences.zh: 彭城王紱上言，樂賢堂有先帝手畫佛象，經歷寇難，而此堂猶存，宜敕作頌。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Fan submitted a statement that in the Hall for Honoring Worthies there was a Buddha image drawn by the hand of the former emperor; through invasions and disaster that hall still stood; he asked that an edict command composition of a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Pengcheng noted that the Hall for Honoring Worthies still housed a Buddha sketch by a late emperor despite wartime damage, and asked for a commemorative ode.

sentences.zh: 帝下其議。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the matter down for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred it for discussion.

sentences.zh: 謨曰：「佛者，夷狄之俗，非經典之制。

translations.literal: Mo said, "The Buddha is a custom of the Yi and Di; it is not regulated in the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo answered, "Buddhism is a barbarian cult, not sanctioned by the canon."

sentences.zh: 先帝量同天地，多才多藝，聊因臨時而畫此象，至於雅好佛道，所未承聞也。

translations.literal: The former emperors were vast as heaven and earth, with many talents and many arts; sketching this image idly on the moment is not the same as having refined love for Buddha's way—your servant has not heard that they did.
translations.idiomatic: A late sovereign's genius might indulge a doodle in passing; I have never heard that he meant to embrace Buddhism as a personal faith."

sentences.zh: 盜賊奔突，王都隳敗，而此堂塊然獨存，斯誠神靈保祚之征，然未是大晉盛德之形容，歌頌之所先也。

translations.literal: Bandits rampaged and the royal capital was wrecked, yet this hall alone stood solid—this is truly an omen of spirits protecting the blessing, yet it is not yet a description of the great Jin's magnificent virtue, nor what eulogy ought to take first.
translations.idiomatic: That one hall survived massacres may mark divine favor, but it is hardly the foremost symbol of Jin's civilizing virtue for court poets to celebrate.

sentences.zh: 人臣睹物興義，私作賦頌可也。

translations.literal: When subjects see a thing and raise its meaning, private composition of fu and eulogies is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If private gentlemen wish to compose verses on their own, that is fine.

sentences.zh: 今欲發王命，敕史官，上稱先帝好佛之志，下為夷狄作一象之頌，於義有疑焉。

translations.literal: Now one wishes to issue a royal command, charge the historiographers, above praise the former emperor's intent to favor Buddha, below for the Yi and Di compose a eulogy on behalf of a single image—in righteousness there is doubt.
translations.idiomatic: To issue an edict and tell historians to laud a dead emperor's Buddhist taste and to praise a barbarian cult for a sketch sits ill with public duty."

sentences.zh: 」於是遂寢。

translations.literal: Therefore in the end it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時征西將軍庾亮以石勒新死，欲移鎮石城，為滅賊之漸。

translations.literal: At the time General Who Guards the West Yu Liang, because Shi Le had newly died, wished to shift his headquarters to Stone City as a first step toward destroying the foe.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the West Yu Liang, learning of Shi Le's death, wanted to advance his base to Stone City as the opening move against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 事下公卿。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor circulated the plan to the high ministers.

sentences.zh: 謨議曰：

translations.literal: Mo delivered a deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo answered in a long memorial:

sentences.zh: 時有否泰，道有屈伸，暴逆之寇雖終滅亡，然當其強盛，皆屈而避之。

translations.literal: The times have their bad and good fortune; the Way has its bends and straightness; though violent rebels are finally extinguished, when they are at their strongest everyone bends low and avoids them.
translations.idiomatic: History moves between crisis and calm; strategy must bend and stretch. Even doomed rebels must be dodged when their storm is fiercest.

sentences.zh: 是以高祖受黜于巴漢，忍辱于平城也。

translations.literal: Therefore the High Founder suffered dismissal in Ba and Han and endured humiliation at Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Han Gaozu endured exile in Ba-Han and shame at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 若爭強於鴻門，則亡不終日。

translations.literal: If he had vied for victory at Hong Gate he would not have survived the day.
translations.idiomatic: Had he forced a showdown at Hong Gate he would not have lasted a day.

sentences.zh: 故蕭何曰「百戰百敗，不死何待」也。

translations.literal: Therefore Xiao He said, 'A hundred fights, a hundred defeats—if you do not die, what are you waiting for?'
translations.idiomatic: As Xiao He warned, "Win every skirmish and still lose the war—what then but death?"

sentences.zh: 原始要終，歸於大濟而已。

translations.literal: Probing the origin and grasping the end, one returns to great rescue—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The point is the final rescue of the realm, not momentary pride.

sentences.zh: 豈與當亡之寇爭遲速之間哉！

translations.literal: How can one with a foe about to perish contest the interval between slow and fast!
translations.idiomatic: Why wrestle a dying enemy over who moves faster?

sentences.zh: 夫惟鴻門之不爭，故垓下莫能與之爭。

translations.literal: Only because Hong Gate was not contested could none beneath Gaixia vie with him.
translations.idiomatic: Precisely because Gaozu skipped Hong Gate, no rival could face him at Gaixia.

sentences.zh: 文王身圮於羑裏，故道泰於牧野；

translations.literal: King Wen personally fell low at Youli; therefore the Way flourished at Muye;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen suffered captivity at Youli so the Mandate could blaze at Muye;

sentences.zh: 句踐見屈於會稽，故威申于強吳。

translations.literal: Goujian was humbled at Mount Kuaiji; therefore his might extended through mighty Wu.
translations.idiomatic: King Goujian bowed at Kuaiji so his armies could humble strong Wu.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，亦由此矣。

translations.literal: Today's affair arises from the same logic.
translations.idiomatic: Our situation follows the same logic.

sentences.zh: 賊假息之命垂盡，而豺狼之力尚強；

translations.literal: The bandit draws borrowed breath and his allotted span is nearly gone, yet the strength of wolves and jackals is still fierce;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu clings to borrowed time—he is dying—yet his wolves still bite hard;

sentences.zh: 宜抗威以待時。

translations.literal: one ought to raise awe-inspiring might and await the moment.
translations.idiomatic: we should brandish strength and bide the right moment.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「抗威待時，時已可矣。

translations.literal: Someone may say, 'Raise might and wait—the moment is already ripe.'
translations.idiomatic: Some say the moment is ripe already.

sentences.zh: 」愚以為時之可否在賊之強弱，賊之強弱在季龍之能否。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that whether the time is ripe lies in the enemy's strength or weakness; the enemy's strength or weakness lies in whether Jilong (Shi Hu) can hold his house together.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the hour has struck depends on how strong Zhao remains, and that rests on whether Shi Hu can still dominate his court.

sentences.zh: 季龍之能否，可得而言矣。

translations.literal: Whether Jilong can or cannot may be stated.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's ability is plain from the record alone.

sentences.zh: 自勒初起，則季龍為爪牙，百戰百勝，遂定中國，境土所據，同于魏世。

translations.literal: From the time Le first rose, Jilong was his claws and fangs; a hundred fights, a hundred victories, and he settled the Middle Kingdom; territory occupied matches Wei times.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shi Le's first rising, Shi Hu has been his cutting edge—undefeated until the heartland was theirs—controlling ground comparable to Wei at its height.

sentences.zh: 及勒死之日，將相內外欲誅季龍。

translations.literal: On the day Le died, generals and ministers inside and out wished to execute Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le died, every minister in Luoyang wanted Shi Hu dead.

sentences.zh: 季龍獨起於眾異之中，殺嗣主，誅寵臣。

translations.literal: Jilong alone rose from the mass of rivals, killed the heir, purged favored ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu rose alone among the factions, murdered the heir, and slaughtered the inner favorites.

sentences.zh: 內難既定，千里遠出，一攻而拔金墉，再戰而斬石生，禽彭彪，殺石聰，滅郭權，還據根本，內外並定，四方鎮守，不失尺土。

translations.literal: Once internal disaster was settled, he marched a thousand li, took Gold Citadel at one blow, in a second battle beheaded Shi Sheng, captured Peng Biao, killed Shi Cong, annihilated Guo Quan, returned to hold his base, settled inner and outer together, guarded every quarter, and lost not a foot of soil.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched a thousand miles, seized Gold Citadel, killed Shi Sheng in the field, took Peng Biao, executed Shi Cong, wiped out Guo Quan, secured his base, pacified every garrison, and lost no territory.

sentences.zh: 詳察此事，豈能乎，將不能也？

translations.literal: Examine this affair minutely—could he do it, or could he not?
translations.idiomatic: Study that track record: could he pull it off or not?

sentences.zh: 假令不能者為之，其將濟乎，將不濟也？

translations.literal: Suppose one who could not had undertaken it—would he succeed, or would he not?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a lesser man tries again—will he succeed?

sentences.zh: 賊前襄陽而不能拔，誠有之矣。

translations.literal: That the bandits earlier could not take Xiangyang is indeed true.
translations.idiomatic: It is true they once failed at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 不信百戰之效，而執一攻之驗，棄多從少，于理安乎？

translations.literal: To disbelieve the lesson of a hundred campaigns yet cling to the evidence of a single assault, discarding the many and following the few—is it reasonable in principle?
translations.idiomatic: But to ignore a hundred proofs and seize on one failure, trusting rarity over pattern—does that make sense?

sentences.zh: 譬若射者，百發而一不中，可謂之拙乎？

translations.literal: Again, if an archer misses once in a hundred shots, may he be called clumsy?
translations.idiomatic: If an archer misses once in a hundred draws, do we call him a fool?

sentences.zh: 且不拔襄陽者，非季龍身也。

translations.literal: Moreover the failure to take Xiangyang was not because Jilong went in person.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Shi Hu never led that siege of Xiangyang himself.

sentences.zh: 桓平北，守邊之將耳。

translations.literal: Huan the Pacifier of the North was only a frontier warden.
translations.idiomatic: General Huan Xuanzhi was merely a border commander.

sentences.zh: 賊前攻之，爭疆埸耳，得之為善，不得則止，非其所急也。

translations.literal: When the bandits attacked before, they wrangled over border marches; if they won it was good, if not they stopped—it was not what they urgently needed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao army had fenced for border gains, advancing when they could and stopping when they could not—it was never a do-or-die thrust.

sentences.zh: 今征西之往，則異於是。

translations.literal: Now if the general who guards the west goes thither it will differ from this.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang's proposed move is something else entirely.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is that?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 重鎮也，名賢也，中國之人所聞而歸心也。

translations.literal: A key fortress, a famed worthy—men of the Middle Kingdom have heard of him and lean hearts toward him.
translations.idiomatic: It is a strategic choke point garrisoned by a celebrated commander whom the world already trusts.

sentences.zh: 今而西度，實有席捲河南之勢，賊所大懼，豈與桓宣同哉！

translations.literal: If now he crosses west there is truly a momentum to roll up Henan; it is what the bandits greatly fear—how can it be the same as Huan Xuanzhi!
translations.idiomatic: Westward advance under Yu Liang would look like a sweep through Henan—the very nightmare of Zhao—nothing like Huan's border skirmish.

sentences.zh: 季龍必率其精兵，身來距爭。

translations.literal: Jilong will certainly lead picked troops in person to block the contest.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu will march his elites in person to bar the way.

sentences.zh: 若欲與戰，戰何如石生？

translations.literal: If you wish to give battle, how does your battle compare to facing Shi Sheng?
translations.idiomatic: If we fight, can we beat Shi Sheng's defense?

sentences.zh: 若欲城守，守何如金墉？

translations.literal: If you wish to fortify and defend, how does your defense compare to Gold Citadel?
translations.idiomatic: If we sit behind walls, can we hold better than Gold Citadel did?

sentences.zh: 若欲阻沔，沔何如大江？

translations.literal: If you wish to block the Han River, how does the Han compare to the Great River?
translations.idiomatic: If we try to block the Han, is that barrier like the Yangzi?

sentences.zh: 蘇峻何如季龍？

translations.literal: How does Su Jun compare to Jilong?
translations.idiomatic: Was Su Jun half as dangerous as Shi Hu?

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，宜群校之。

translations.literal: Concerning these several points, they ought to be weighed together by the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: These points belong in one calculation for the council.

sentences.zh: 愚謂石生猛將，關中精兵，征西之虎不能勝也。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that Shi Sheng was a fierce commander with crack troops from Guanzhong, yet the tiger strength of the general who guards the west could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng commanded Guanzhong elites; even Yu Liang's "tiger" host could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 金墉險固，劉曜十萬所不能拔，今征西之守不能勝也。

translations.literal: Gold Citadel's precipitous strength Liu Yao's hundred thousand could not take; yet the general who guards the west's defense could not overcome it.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand of Liu Yao could not storm Gold Citadel; Yu Liang is no surer shield.

sentences.zh: 又是時兗州、洛陽、關中皆舉兵擊季龍。

translations.literal: Moreover at that time Yan province, Luoyang, and Guanzhong all raised troops against Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yan, Luoyang, and Guanzhong then all attacked Shi Hu together.

sentences.zh: 今此三處反為其用，方之於前，倍半之覺也。

translations.literal: Now those three zones instead serve him; compared with earlier the danger has more than doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Now those regions feed his war machine—our peril is doubled.

sentences.zh: 若石生不能敵其半，而征西欲當其倍，愚所疑也。

translations.literal: If Shi Sheng could not withstand half that pressure yet the general who guards the west thinks he can face its double, your servant doubts it.
translations.idiomatic: If Shi Sheng buckled under half that weight, how can Yu Liang bear twice as much?

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之強，不及季龍，沔水之險，不及大江。

translations.literal: Su Jun was not as strong as Jilong; the Han's hazard does not match the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun was weaker than Shi Hu; the Han is no Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 大江不能禦蘇峻，而以沔水禦季龍，又所疑也。

translations.literal: The Great River could not stop Su Jun—yet we would stop Jilong with the Han water—again your servant doubts it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi failed to hold Su Jun—why expect the Han to hold Shi Hu?

sentences.zh: 昔祖士稚在譙，佃於城北，慮賊來攻，因以為資，故豫安軍屯，以禦其外。

translations.literal: Formerly when Zu Shizhi was at Qiao, he farmed north of the city, fearing raiders would strike, and used it as preparation, therefore beforehand set army camps to guard the outer side.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti once farmed north of Qiao, planted camps to shield the fields, and readied for raiders.

sentences.zh: 穀將熟，賊果至，丁夫戰於外，老弱獲於內，多持炬火，急則燒穀而走。

translations.literal: When grain was nearly ripe the bandits indeed came; able-bodied males fought outside while the old and weak harvested within, carrying many torches so that if pressed they burned the grain and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When harvest neared, raiders came; young men fought on the perimeter while women and elders reaped inside, torches ready to burn the crop and flee if pressed.

sentences.zh: 如此數年，竟不得其利。

translations.literal: Thus for several years in the end they obtained no profit.
translations.idiomatic: After years of this they still gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 是時賊唯據沔北，方之於今，四分之一耳。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits only held the north bank of the Han; compared with today it was a quarter of the present threat.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then held only the Han's north bank—a fraction of today's front.

sentences.zh: 士稚不能捍其一，而征西欲禦其四，又所疑也。

translations.literal: Shizhi could not withstand the one part yet the general who guards the west thinks he can withstand four parts—again your servant doubts it.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti could not master a quarter of this threat; can Yu Liang endure four times as much?

sentences.zh: 或云：「賊若多來，則必無糧。

translations.literal: Someone may say, 'If the bandits come in great numbers they must lack grain.'
translations.idiomatic: Some argue a large Zhao host would run out of grain.

sentences.zh: 」然致糧之難，莫過崤函。

translations.literal: Yet no supply hardship exceeds Yao and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no supply line is harder than the Yao-Han passes.

sentences.zh: 而季龍昔涉此險，深入敵國，平關中而後還。

translations.literal: Yet Jilong once crossed that peril, penetrated deep into enemy lands, pacified Guanzhong, and afterward returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu once marched those gorges, cut deep into hostile ground, subdued Guanzhong, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 今至襄陽，路既無險，又行其國內，自相供給，方之於前，難易百倍。

translations.literal: Now to reach Xiangyang the road has no such peril, and moreover he marches within his own realm with internal mutual supply; compared with before the ease or difficulty differs a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: The road to Xiangyang is open; moving inside Zhao he feeds his army from home soil—logistics are a hundredfold easier than before.

sentences.zh: 前已經至難，而謂今不能濟其易，又所疑也。

translations.literal: Earlier he already mastered the hardest task yet one says today he cannot manage the easy—again your servant doubts it.
translations.idiomatic: Having mastered the harder march, why assume he cannot manage the easier?

sentences.zh: 然此所論，但說征西既至之後耳，尚未論道路之慮也。

translations.literal: Yet this discussion only speaks of after the general who guards the west has arrived; it has not yet discussed worries about the road.
translations.idiomatic: This even assumes Yu Liang reaches his objective—route hazards remain unmentioned.

sentences.zh: 自沔以西，水急岸高，魚貫溯流，首尾百里。

translations.literal: West of the Han the water is swift and the banks high; in single file they must ascend the current—a hundred li from head to tail.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Han the current runs fast between high banks; boats must nose upstream in single file for a hundred miles.

sentences.zh: 若賊無宋襄之義，及我未陣而擊之，將如之何？

translations.literal: If the bandits lack the righteousness of Duke Xiang of Song and strike us before we have formed ranks, what then?
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao strikes before we can form line, with no chivalric scruples, what becomes of us?

sentences.zh: 今王士與賊，水陸異勢，便習不同。

translations.literal: Now royal troops and bandits differ in water versus land convenience; practiced skills are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Our men differ from theirs in what maneuvers we know—river versus plain.

sentences.zh: 寇若送死，雖開江延敵，以一當千，猶吞之有餘，宜誘而致之，以保萬全。

translations.literal: If the raiders seek death, though we open the river and invite them in, one of ours for a thousand of theirs still swallows them with surplus; we ought to lure them to come to preserve sure completeness.
translations.idiomatic: If they charge recklessly, we can absorb them even at ten-to-one odds by opening the river line—we should bait them in for a safe kill.

sentences.zh: 棄江遠進，以我所短擊彼所長，懼非廟勝之算。

translations.literal: To abandon the river and thrust deep, striking their strength with our shortness, your servant fears this is not a plan for temple victory.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the river barrier and strike their strength with our weakness is not what the ancestral shrine would advise.

sentences.zh: 朝議同之，故亮不果移鎮。

translations.literal: Court deliberation agreed with him; therefore Liang in the end did not carry out shifting headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The council concurred, and Yu Liang dropped the relocation.

sentences.zh: 初，皇后每年拜陵，勞費甚多，謨建議曰：「古者皇后廟見而已，不拜陵也。

translations.literal: At first, because the empress each year visited the imperial tombs at great labor and expense, Mo proposed, saying, "In antiquity the empress only honored the imperial shrines at temple audience and did not visit tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when the empress yearly toured the tombs at crippling expense, Cai Mo cited antiquity: the empress worshipped only within the ancestral shrines, not in the fields.

sentences.zh: 」由是遂止。

translations.literal: On this account it then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The practice stopped.

sentences.zh: 初，太尉郗鑒疾篤，出謨為太尉軍司，加侍中。

translations.literal: At first, when Grand Commandant Xi Jian was gravely ill, Mo was sent out as military overseer to the grand commandant with attendant-in-ordinary added.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Xi Jian lay dying, Cai Mo was seconded as army director on his staff with attendant-in-ordinary added.

sentences.zh: 鑒卒，即拜謨為征北將軍、都督徐兗青三州揚州之晉陵豫州之沛郡諸軍事、領徐州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Mo was at once appointed general who campaigns north, area commander for military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces plus Jinling in Yang province plus Pei commandery in Yu province, concurrent inspector of Xu province, with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Jian died, Cai Mo became general who campaigns north, area commander over Xu, Yan, Qing, Jinling within Yang, and Pei in Yu, with inspector's authority over Xu and credential staff.

sentences.zh: 時左衛將軍陳光上疏請伐胡，詔令攻壽陽，謨上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time General of the Left Guard Chen Guang submitted a memorial requesting to campaign against the Hu; an edict ordered attack on Shouyang; Mo submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Then Left Guard general Chen Guang urged a strike on the barbarians; an edict fixed on Shouyang; Cai Mo answered with a memorial:

sentences.zh: 今壽陽城小而固。

translations.literal: Now Shouyang city is small yet solid.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang is compact but its walls are strong.

sentences.zh: 自幫陽至琅邪，城壁相望，其間遠者裁百餘里，一城見攻，眾城必救。

translations.literal: From Xiangyang to Langye city walls face one another; among them the farthest is barely more than a hundred li—if one city is attacked, the host of cities must relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiangyang east to Langye, walled towns stand shoulder to shoulder—barely a hundred miles apart—so a strike on one draws relief from every neighbor.

sentences.zh: 且王師在路五十餘日，劉仕一軍早已入淮，又遣數部北取堅壁，大軍未至，聲息久聞。

translations.literal: Moreover the royal army has been on the road more than fifty days; Liu Shi's column long since entered the Huai, and several other detachments have been sent north to seize strongpoints; long before the great host arrives the news will have been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Our columns have marched fifty days; Liu Shi is already in the Huai line, other units are peeling off to seize forts—word will reach Zhao long before the main body closes in.

sentences.zh: 而賊之郵驛，一日千里，河北之騎足以來赴，非惟鄰城相救而已。

translations.literal: Yet the bandits' post relays travel a thousand li a day; cavalry north of the Yellow River suffices to come to the rescue—not only neighboring cities aiding one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's courier relays cover a thousand miles a day; northern cavalry can reinforce every garrison—not merely the next town over.

sentences.zh: 夫以白起、韓信、項籍之勇，猶發梁焚舟，背水而陣。

translations.literal: Now even with the courage of Bai Qi, Han Xin, and Xiang Ji, they still tore up bridges and burned boats and formed ranks with their backs to the water.
translations.idiomatic: Even Bai Qi, Han Xin, and Xiang Yu burned their boats and fought with backs to the river.

sentences.zh: 今欲停船水渚，引兵造城，前對堅敵，顧臨歸路，此兵法之所誡也。

translations.literal: Now you wish to moor boats at mid-river shallows, lead troops to build against the city, face a hardened foe in front and look back on the road of retreat—this is what military arts warn against.
translations.idiomatic: To anchor midstream, march on the city, fight elite troops ahead while the retreat route yawns astern is exactly what every manual forbids.

sentences.zh: 若進攻未拔，胡騎卒至，懼桓子不知所為，而舟中之指可掬。

translations.literal: If the advance attack is not taken and Hu cavalry suddenly arrives, one fears Huan Zi will not know what to do, and the fingers in the boat could be scooped up.
translations.idiomatic: If the siege stalls and Zhao horse arrive overnight, we may relive Duke Huan's panic at dense—fingers enough to fill a boat scooped from the water.

sentences.zh: 今征軍五千，皆王都精銳之眾，又光為左衛，遠近聞之，名為殿中之軍，宜令所向有征無戰。

translations.literal: Now the expeditionary army of five thousand are all picked elite from the royal capital; moreover Guang serves as left guard—far and near hearing this call it the army from within the halls; it ought to be that wherever they go there is conquest without battle.
translations.idiomatic: These five thousand are the capital's picked household guards—Chen Guang's own left-guard veterans—famed as the palace corps; they should march to sure victory.

sentences.zh: 而頓之堅城之下，勝之不武，不勝為笑。

translations.literal: Yet to halt them beneath a hard city—if victorious it is not martial glory; if defeated it becomes a laughingstock.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pinning them under a fortress wall makes even victory petty and defeat a public joke.

sentences.zh: 今以國之上駟擊寇之下邑，得之則利薄而不足損敵，失之則害重而足以益寇，懼非策之長者。

translations.literal: Now to strike the bandits' lower towns with the state's top teams—if you gain them the profit is thin and insufficient to harm the foe; if you lose them the harm is weighty and enough to strengthen the bandits—your servant fears this is not the long plan of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Using our best troops on Zhao's second-tier towns yields little if we win and costs dearly if we lose—hardly sound strategy.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為聞寇而致討，賊退而振旅，於事無失。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that hearing of the bandits then launching punishment, and when the bandits withdraw shaking the troops, in affairs loses nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike when raiders appear and stand down when they withdraw—nothing lost by that rhythm.

sentences.zh: 不勝管見，謹冒陳聞。

translations.literal: Unable to exhaust narrow views, reverently risk laying them before the hearing.
translations.idiomatic: These are crude thoughts offered in earnest.

sentences.zh: 季龍於青州造船數百，掠緣海諸縣，所在殺戮，朝廷以為憂。

translations.literal: Jilong at Qingzhou built several hundred ships, raided counties along the sea, slaughtering wherever he went; the court took this as worry.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu built hundreds of warships in Qingzhou and harried the coast, slaughtering as he went; the court was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 謨遣龍驤將軍徐玄等守中洲，並設募，若得賊大白船者，賞布千匹，小船百匹。

translations.literal: Mo dispatched General Who Prances the Dragon Xu Xuan and others to guard Central Isle and likewise set up recruitment: if one captured a bandit great white ship, reward a thousand bolts of cloth; small ships a hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo sent General Who Prances the Dragon Xu Xuan to hold Central Isle and offered a bounty—one thousand bolts for a large enemy hull, a hundred for a small craft.

sentences.zh: 是時謨所統七千餘人，所戍東至土山，西至江乘，鎮守八所，城壘凡十一處，烽火樓望三十餘處，隨宜防備，甚有算略。

translations.literal: At this time those under Mo's command were more than seven thousand; garrisons stretched east to Mount Tu and west to Jiangcheng; he guarded eight posts with eleven walled camps and more than thirty beacon watchtowers, adapting defenses as fit—very much possessed of calculation and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded seven thousand men in eight sectors from Mount Tu to Jiangcheng—eleven forts and thirty beacon towers—each post tailored to terrain with evident tactical sense.

sentences.zh: 先是，郗鑒上部下有勳勞者凡一百八十人，帝並酬其功，未卒而鑒薨，斷不復與。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi Jian had listed subordinates with merit totaling one hundred eighty persons; the emperor had all rewarded their merit, but before it was completed Jian died, and the grants were cut off and not continued.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian had nominated 180 men for merit pay; the throne had approved, but his death left the roster unpaid.

sentences.zh: 謨上疏以為先已許鑒，今不宜斷。

translations.literal: Mo submitted a memorial holding that since promise had already been made to Jian, now it was not appropriate to cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo argued that a pledge to Xi Jian must not be broken midstream.

sentences.zh: 且鑒所上者皆積年勳效，百戰之餘，亦不可不報。

translations.literal: Moreover those whom Jian submitted all had years of accumulated merit and effect, survivors of a hundred battles—it is also not possible not to repay them.
translations.idiomatic: These were veterans of a hundred fights—denying them reward would be unjust.

sentences.zh: 詔聽之。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 康帝即位，徵拜左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang ascended the throne, Mo was summoned as left grand household, bearer of the golden seal and purple ribbon, concurrent minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang named him left grand household with three-excellency honors while keeping him as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 代殷浩為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: He replaced Yin Hao as inspector of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Yin Hao as inspector of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 又錄尚書事，領司徒如故。

translations.literal: Again he recorded overseer business for the secretariat; concurrent minister of education as before.
translations.idiomatic: He also took the recording overseer portfolio while remaining minister of education.

sentences.zh: 初，謨沖讓不辟僚佐，詔屢敦逼之，始取掾屬。

translations.literal: At first Mo was modest and would not summon subordinate officials; edicts repeatedly pressed him harshly, and he then began to take clerks and staff.
translations.idiomatic: At first Cai Mo refused to build a private staff until repeated edicts forced him to appoint clerks.

sentences.zh: 石季龍死，中國大亂。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong died, the Middle Kingdom was greatly in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's death threw the north into chaos.

sentences.zh: 時朝野咸謂當太平復舊，謨獨謂不然，語所親曰：「胡滅，誠大慶也，然將貽王室之憂。

translations.literal: At the time court and countryside all said there would be peace and restoration of the old order; Mo alone said it was not so, telling those close to him, "When the Hu are destroyed it is indeed a great blessing, yet it will hand trouble to the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Court and country assumed peace would follow; Cai Mo alone told friends that crushing the barbarians would bring new woes for the throne.

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「何哉？

translations.literal: Someone said, "How so?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked why.

sentences.zh: 」謨曰：「夫能順天而奉時，濟六合於草昧，若非上哲，必由英豪。

translations.literal: Mo said, "He who can obey Heaven and serve the times, aiding the six regions in the grass-blind dawn, if he is not a supreme sage must be a heroic champion.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "To reunite the realm from chaos takes either a sage-king or a conquering hero.

sentences.zh: 度德量力，非時賢所及。

translations.literal: Measuring virtue and weighing strength are not what the worthies of the age can match.
translations.idiomatic: Our present worthies lack both the virtue and the strength for it.

sentences.zh: 必將經營分表，疲人以逞志。

translations.literal: They will surely extend operations beyond the proper bounds, wearing out the people to satisfy ambition.
translations.idiomatic: They will overreach, exhaust the people, and chase private ambition.

sentences.zh: 才不副意，略不稱心，財單力竭，智勇俱屈，此韓廬、東郭所以雙斃也。」

translations.literal: When talent does not match intent and strategy does not match the heart, resources run dry and strength is exhausted, wisdom and courage both bend—this is why Han's hound and Dongguo both perished together."
translations.idiomatic: When ability falls short of aim, funds run dry, nerve fails—both hunter and hound collapse together, as in the old fable."

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、司徒。

translations.literal: He was moved to attendant-in-ordinary and minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary while remaining minister of education.

sentences.zh: 上疏讓曰：「伏自惟省，昔階謬恩，蒙忝非據，屍素累積而光寵更崇，謗讟彌興而榮進復加，上虧聖朝棟隆之舉，下增微臣覆餗之釁，惶懼戰灼，寄顏無所。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial declining, saying, "Prostrate, your servant examines himself: formerly stepping on mistaken favor he disgracefully occupied a post beyond his station; corpse-like slack piled up yet dazzling favor grew ever loftier; slander swelled yet glory and advancement were again added—above injuring the sagely court's raising of ridgepole timber, below increasing your servant's fault of overturning the stew—fearful and burning, he has nowhere to set his face.
translations.idiomatic: He begged off again, citing unworthiness, mounting scandal, and fear of shaming the court's choice of pillars.

sentences.zh: 乞垂天鑒，回恩改謬，以允群望。

translations.literal: Beg that Heaven's mirror bend down, turn favor and correct error, so as to satisfy the multitude's expectation."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the throne to withdraw the appointment and satisfy public opinion."

sentences.zh: 」皇太后詔報不許。

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued an edict in reply not permitting.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Chu refused.

sentences.zh: 謨猶固讓，謂所親曰：「我若為司徒，將為後代所哂，義不敢拜也。

translations.literal: Mo still firmly declined, telling those close to him, "If I become minister of education, later generations will ridicule me; in righteousness I dare not accept the investiture."
translations.idiomatic: He told friends, "If I take the ministry of education, posterity will laugh—I cannot in good conscience accept."

sentences.zh: 」皇太后遣使喻意，自四年冬至五年末，詔書屢下，謨固守所執。

translations.literal: The empress dowager dispatched envoys to explain her intent; from the fourth year's winter to the fifth year's end edicts came down repeatedly, yet Mo firmly held to what he grasped.
translations.idiomatic: From winter of the fourth year to the end of the fifth year she sent messengers urging him; he still refused.

sentences.zh: 六年，復上疏，以疾病乞骸骨，上左光祿大夫、領司徒印綬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again submitted a memorial, because of illness begging for his bones and returning the seals of left grand household and concurrent minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he pleaded illness, asked to retire, and returned the seals of left grand household and minister of education.

sentences.zh: 章表十餘上。

translations.literal: Memorials and tables came to more than ten submissions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent more than ten memorials to the same effect.

sentences.zh: 穆帝臨軒，遣侍中紀璩、黃門郎丁纂征謨。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu faced the hall and dispatched Attendant-in-ordinary Ji Quan and Gentleman at the Yellow Gates Ding Zuan to summon Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu held audience and sent Ji Quan and Ding Zuan to fetch Cai Mo to court.

sentences.zh: 謨陳疾篤，使主簿謝攸對曰：「臣謨不幸有公族穆子之疾，天威不違顏咫尺，不敢奉詔，寢伏待罪。

translations.literal: Mo stated grave illness and had chief clerk Xie You reply, saying, "Your servant Mo unhappily has the ailment of the ducal house's Muzi; Heaven's majesty does not withdraw a span from the face; he does not dare obey the edict and lies prostrate awaiting punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo pleaded the chronic illness of Zhao Muzi of Jin, said he dared not face the Son of Heaven, and sent his chief clerk to beg leave while awaiting censure.

sentences.zh: 」自旦至申，使者十餘反，而謨不至。

translations.literal: From dawn to mid-afternoon the envoys went back and forth more than ten times, yet Mo did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Messengers shuttled more than ten times from dawn past noon; Cai Mo never appeared.

sentences.zh: 時帝年八歲，甚倦，問左右曰：「所召人何以至今不來？

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was eight years old and very weary; he asked those at his side, "Why has the man summoned still not come?"
translations.idiomatic: The eight-year-old emperor wearied and asked why the minister had not come.

sentences.zh: 臨軒何時當竟？

translations.literal: When will facing the hall finally finish?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked when the audience would end."

sentences.zh: 」君臣俱疲弊。

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers alike were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Court and throne were exhausted alike.

sentences.zh: 皇太后詔：「必不來者，宜罷朝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager edicted, "If he is determined not to come, it is appropriate to dismiss court."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered court suspended if Cai Mo stayed away.

sentences.zh: 」中軍將軍殷浩奏免吏部尚書江虨官。

translations.literal: General of the central army Yin Hao memorialized to dismiss Minister of Personnel Jiang Bin from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao impeached Minister of Personnel Jiang Bin.

sentences.zh: 簡文時為會稽王，命曹曰：「蔡公傲違上命，無人臣之禮。

translations.literal: Prince of Kuaiji, later Emperor Jianwen, ordered his office, saying, "Lord Cai arrogantly disobeys supreme command and lacks the ritual of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yu of Kuaiji declared that Cai Mo had defied the sovereign and abandoned ministerial duty.

sentences.zh: 若人主卑屈于上，大義不行於下，亦不知復所以為政矣。

translations.literal: If the ruler humbles himself above while great righteousness does not proceed below, your servant also does not know how thereafter to conduct government."
translations.idiomatic: If the throne bows while ministers withhold respect, government cannot continue."

sentences.zh: 」於是公卿奏曰：「司徒謨頃以常疾，久逋王命，皇帝臨軒，百僚齊立，俯僂之恭，有望於謨，若志存止退，自宜致辭闕庭，安有人君卑勞終日而人臣曾無一酬之禮！

translations.literal: Thereupon dukes and ministers memorialized, saying, "Minister of Education Mo recently because of constant illness has long evaded royal command; the emperor faces the hall and the hundred officials stand in order; the bowed humility was directed toward Mo—if his intent were to stop and retire, he ought himself to have presented his words at the palace gate—how can there be a ruler laboring humbly all day while the minister never once answers with the ritual of thanks!"
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers charged Cai Mo with leaving the boy emperor standing all day while he hid at home.

sentences.zh: 悖慢傲上，罪同不臣。

translations.literal: Rebellious slowness and arrogance toward the sovereign; the crime equals not being a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Such arrogance toward the throne is tantamount to treason.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，宜明國憲，請送廷尉，以正刑書。

translations.literal: Your servants jointly deliberate that the state statutes ought to be clarified; we ask to send him to the minister of trials so as to correct the penal texts."
translations.idiomatic: They moved to remand him to the minister of trials for sentencing."

sentences.zh: 」謨懼，率子弟素服詣闕稽顙，躬到廷尉待罪。

translations.literal: Mo feared, led sons and younger kin in undyed garments to the palace gate knocking foreheads, and personally went to the minister of trials awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo relented, led his family in mourning dress to the palace gate, and surrendered to the minister of trials.

sentences.zh: 皇太后詔曰：「謨先帝師傅，服事累世。

translations.literal: The empress dowager edicted, saying, "Mo was tutor to former emperors and has served through successive reigns.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager replied that Cai Mo had tutored two emperors and served many years.

sentences.zh: 且歸罪有司，內訟思愆。

translations.literal: Moreover he has returned blame to the offices and inwardly sues himself thinking of faults.
translations.idiomatic: He had humbled himself before the law and repented.

sentences.zh: 若遂致之於理，情所未忍。

translations.literal: If in the end he is handed over to principle, in feeling your servant cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: She could not bear to jail him formally.

sentences.zh: 可依舊制免為庶人。」

translations.literal: May follow old institutions and dismiss him to commoner status."
translations.idiomatic: She stripped him of rank but spared his life."

sentences.zh: 謨既被廢，杜門不出，終日講誦，教授子弟。

translations.literal: After Mo was dismissed, he shut his gates and did not go out, all day lecturing and reciting, teaching sons and younger kin.
translations.idiomatic: Disgraced, Cai Mo stayed home, teaching his children and reading.

sentences.zh: 數年，皇太后詔曰：「前司徒謨以道素著稱，軌行成名，故曆事先朝，致位台輔，以往年之失，用致黜責。

translations.literal: After several years the empress dowager edicted, saying, "Former Minister of Education Mo by the Way and plainness was famed; by rule and conduct he completed his name; therefore he served former courts in sequence and reached the ministerial summit; because of last year's fault he suffered dismissal and rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Years later she cited his old virtue and past service, blaming only his recent refusal.

sentences.zh: 自爾已來，闔門思愆，誠合大臣罪己之義。

translations.literal: Since then he has closed his gate thinking of faults; this truly matches the great ministers' meaning of blaming themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since then he had shut his doors in repentance, as great ministers should.

sentences.zh: 以謨為光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Appoint Mo grand household of the palace revenues, bearer of the golden seal and purple ribbon."
translations.idiomatic: She restored him as grand household with three-excellency honors."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣謁者僕射孟洪就加冊命。

translations.literal: Thereupon she dispatched Herald Commandant Meng Hong to go confer the patent of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Herald Meng Hong brought the patent to his house.

sentences.zh: 謨上疏陳謝曰：「臣以頑薄，皆忝殊寵，屍素累紀，加違慢詔命，當肆市朝。

translations.literal: Mo submitted a memorial expressing thanks, saying, "Your servant by stubborn meanness has repeatedly disgraced himself with extraordinary favor; corpse-like slack piled up for years; moreover he violated and was slow to imperial edicts—he ought to be exposed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo thanked her in a memorial admitting fault and declaring himself unworthy of renewed favor.

sentences.zh: 幸蒙寬宥，不悟天施復加光飾，非臣隕越所能上報。

translations.literal: Fortunately he received broad forgiveness; he did not expect Heaven's gift again to add luster—this is not what your servant's smashing body can repay upward.
translations.idiomatic: He had expected execution, not restoration.

sentences.zh: 臣寢疾未損，不任詣闕。

translations.literal: Your servant's lying illness is not yet improved; he cannot bear to go to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ill health still kept him from court.

sentences.zh: 不勝仰感聖恩，謹遣拜章。

translations.literal: Unable to master gratitude for sagely favor, reverently he dispatches a memorial with obeisance."
translations.idiomatic: He sent thanks in writing instead."

sentences.zh: 」遂以疾篤，不復朝見。

translations.literal: Thereupon because illness was grave he no longer attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: His illness kept him from audiences thereafter.

sentences.zh: 詔賜几杖，門施行馬。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed a couch, staff, and horse barriers at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a couch, cane, and ceremonial gate barriers.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 356 at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 賵贈之禮，一依太尉陸玩故事。

translations.literal: The gifts for obsequies followed in every case the precedent of Grand Commandant Lu Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral honors matched those given Lu Wan.

sentences.zh: 詔贈侍中、司空，諡曰文穆。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded attendant-in-ordinary and minister of works with the posthumous name Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named attendant-in-ordinary and minister of works with the epithet Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 謨博學，於禮儀宗廟制度多所議定。

translations.literal: Mo was broadly learned; in ritual observance and ancestral temple institutions he deliberated and fixed much.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo was erudite and helped codify court ritual and temple law.

sentences.zh: 文筆論議，有集行於世。

translations.literal: His literary brush and discourses were collected in a compilation circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His essays were collected and published.

sentences.zh: 總應劭以來注班固《漢書》者，為之集解。

translations.literal: He gathered commentators on Ban Gu's Han shu from Ying Shao onward and produced a collected exegesis for them.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a critical edition of Han shu commentary from Ying Shao onward.

sentences.zh: 謨初渡江，見彭蜞，大喜曰：「蟹有八足，加以二螯。

translations.literal: When Mo first crossed the Yangzi he saw river crabs and greatly rejoiced, saying, "Crabs have eight legs plus two claws."
translations.idiomatic: On first crossing south he spotted estuarine crabs and cried, "Eight legs and two claws—just like the classic says of true crabs!"

sentences.zh: 」令烹之。

translations.literal: He ordered them cooked.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them cooked at once.

sentences.zh: 既食，吐下委頓，方知非蟹。

translations.literal: After eating he vomited and collapsed with diarrhea, and then knew they were not crabs.
translations.idiomatic: Violent vomiting taught him they were not edible crabs.

sentences.zh: 後詣謝尚而說之。

translations.literal: Later he visited Xie Shang and told him of it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told Xie Shang the story.

sentences.zh: 尚曰：「卿讀《爾雅》不熟，幾為《勸學》死。

translations.literal: Shang said, "You did not read the Erya carefully and nearly died for the Encourage Learning piece."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang laughed, "Had you studied the Erya you would not have nearly killed yourself on the crab verse from the Encourage Learning school primer."

sentences.zh: 」謨性方雅。

translations.literal: Mo's nature was square and cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo was grave and refined.

sentences.zh: 丞相王導作女伎，施設床席。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wang Dao set up female entertainers and spread out couches and mats.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao once staged female musicians and laid out banquet seats.

sentences.zh: 謨先在坐，不悅而去，導亦不止之。

translations.literal: Mo was already seated among them, displeased departed, and Dao also did not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo, already present, left in disgust; Wang Dao did not call him back.

sentences.zh: 性尤篤慎，每事必為過防。

translations.literal: By nature he was especially earnest and cautious; in every affair he always made excessive precautions.
translations.idiomatic: He was almost comically cautious in every detail.

sentences.zh: 故時人云：「蔡公過浮航，脫帶腰舟。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time said, "When Lord Cai crossed the floating bridge he unstrapped his sash to use as a life belt."
translations.idiomatic: Wits said, "When Lord Cai crossed the pontoon he loosened his sash to double as a life preserver."

sentences.zh: 」長子邵，永嘉太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shao was administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Cai Shao governed Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 少子系，有才學文義，位至撫軍長史。

translations.literal: His youngest son Xi had talent, learning, and literary judgment; his office reached chief clerk to the general who soothes the army.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Cai Xi, a scholar, rose to chief clerk on the staff of the general who soothes the army.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恢

translations.literal: Zhuge Hui
translations.idiomatic: The text next treats Zhuge Hui.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恢，字道明，琅邪陽都人也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Hui, courtesy name Daoming, was a man of Yangdu in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui, courtesy Daoming, came from Yangdu in Langye commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖誕，魏司空，為文帝所誅。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dan was minister of works under Wei and was executed by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhuge Dan had been Wei minister of works and was executed by Cao Rui.

sentences.zh: 父靚，奔吳，為大司馬。

translations.literal: His father Jing fled to Wu and became grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuge Jing fled to Wu and rose to grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 吳平，逃竄不出。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified he fled and hid and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell he stayed in hiding.

sentences.zh: 武帝與靚有舊，靚姊又為琅邪王妃，帝知靚在姊間，因就見焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had old ties with Jing; moreover Jing's elder sister was consort to the prince of Langye; the emperor knew Jing was among his sister's household and therefore went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had known Zhuge Jing in youth, and Jing's sister was consort to the prince of Langye; learning Jing hid with her, the emperor went to see him.

sentences.zh: 靚逃於廁，帝又逼見之，謂曰：「不謂今日復得相見。

translations.literal: Jing fled to the privy; the emperor again forced a meeting and said to him, "I did not expect today again to obtain meeting one another."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing bolted to the privy; Sima Yan cornered him there and said, "I never thought we would meet again."

sentences.zh: 」靚流涕曰：「不能漆身皮面，復睹聖顏！

translations.literal: Jing wept, saying, "I could not smear my body with lacquer nor mask my face with leather, yet again to behold the sage countenance!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing wept, "I could not mutilate myself like Yao Li; I must face your sacred face again."

sentences.zh: 」詔以為侍中，固辭不拜，歸於鄉里，終身不向朝廷而坐。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him attendant-in-ordinary; he firmly declined and did not take office, returned to his home village, and to the end of his life did not sit facing the direction of court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him attendant-in-ordinary; he refused, retired to his village, and never again sat with his back to the north as a subject would.

sentences.zh: 恢弱冠知名，試守即丘長，轉臨沂令，為政和平。

translations.literal: Hui was known while still weak-capped; on probation he was magistrate of Jiqiu, transferred to magistrate of Linyi; his government was peaceful and even.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui was famous before his capping, served as acting magistrate of Jiqiu, then Linyi, governing gently and fairly.

sentences.zh: 值天下大亂，避地江左，名亞王導、庾亮。

translations.literal: Encountering great chaos in the realm, he fled to shelter east of the Yangzi; his name was second to Wang Dao and Yu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed south during the wars, ranked just below Wang Dao and Yu Liang in reputation.

sentences.zh: 導嘗謂曰：「明府當為黑頭公。

translations.literal: Dao once said to him, "My lord will surely become a black-headed minister."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao once told him, "You will die still a black-haired minister of state—still in harness at the top."

sentences.zh: 」及導拜司空，恢在從，導指冠謂曰：「君當復著此。

translations.literal: When Dao was invested minister of works, Hui was in the entourage; Dao pointed to the cap and said to him, "You ought again to wear this."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dao became minister of work, Zhuge Hui stood in his train; Wang Dao tapped his own cap and said, "You will wear this again yourself."

sentences.zh: 」導嘗與恢戲爭族姓，曰：「人言王葛，不言葛王也。

translations.literal: Dao once disputed with Hui in jest over clan surnames, saying, "People say Wang and Ge, they do not say Ge and Wang."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao once teased him about surname precedence: "Everyone says Wang and Ge, never Ge and Wang."

sentences.zh: 」恢曰：「不言馬驢，而言驢馬，豈驢勝馬邪！

translations.literal: Hui said, "They do not say horse and donkey, yet they say donkey and horse—does that mean the donkey surpasses the horse!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui shot back, "People say donkey and horse, not horse and donkey—does that make the donkey the better beast?"

sentences.zh: 」其見親狎如此。

translations.literal: Thus he was treated with such intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the easy familiarity he enjoyed with Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 于時潁川荀闓字道明、陳留蔡謨字道明，與恢俱有名譽，號曰「中興三明」，人為之語曰：「京都三明各有名，蔡氏儒雅荀葛清。」

translations.literal: At the time Xun Kai of Yingchuan, courtesy Daoming, and Cai Mo of Chenliu, courtesy Daoming, together with Hui all had reputation; they were called the "Three Luminaries of the Restoration," and people made a saying: "The three Luminaries of the capital each have their fame—the Cai clan is refined Confucians, the Xun and Ge clans are pure."
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan's Xun Kai, Chenliu's Cai Mo, and Zhuge Hui—each with the courtesy Daoming—were famed as the "Three Bright Men of the Restoration," and a rhyme ran: "Three bright stars shine in the capital: the Cais are cultured, the Xuns and Ges are clear."

sentences.zh: 元帝為安東將軍，以恢為主簿，再遷江寧令。
