translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was general who guards the east, he appointed Hui chief clerk, then twice promoted him magistrate of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: As general who guards the east, Emperor Yuan made Zhuge Hui his chief clerk, then twice promoted him to magistrate of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 討周馥有功，封博陵亭侯，復為鎮東參軍。

translations.literal: For merit in campaigning against Zhou Fu he was enfeoffed village marquis of Boling, again became adjutant to the general who guards the east.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the village marquisate of Boling for helping crush Zhou Fu and returned to the eastern headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 與卞壼並以時譽遷從事中郎，兼統記室。

translations.literal: Together with Bian Kun by timely reputation he was moved retainer clerk, concurrently heading the record office.
translations.idiomatic: He and Bian Kun rose together on reputation to retainer clerk, jointly heading the secretariat record office.

sentences.zh: 時四方多務，箋疏殷積，恢斟酌酬答，咸稱折中。

translations.literal: At the time in the four directions affairs were many; memorials and notes piled thickly; Hui weighed and answered them and all called them balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from every quarter piled up; Zhuge Hui drafted replies that everyone called fair.

sentences.zh: 于時王氏為將軍，而恢兄弟及顏含並居顯要，劉超以忠謹掌書命，時人以帝善任一國之才。

translations.literal: At the time the Wang clan were generals, while Hui's brothers and Yan Han together held eminent posts; Liu Chao by loyalty and care managed written orders; men of the time considered that the emperor was good at employing the talent of a whole state.
translations.idiomatic: The Wangs held military power while Zhuge Hui, his brothers, and Yan Han filled high civil posts; Liu Chao handled edicts with scrupulous care—contemporaries said the emperor knew how to use every kind of talent.

sentences.zh: 湣帝即位，徵用四方賢雋，召恢為尚書郎，元帝以經緯須才，上疏留之，承制調為會稽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, he summoned worthies from the four directions and called Hui to be gentleman in the secretariat; Emperor Yuan, because ordering the realm required talent, submitted a memorial to retain him and by plenipotentiary order transferred him to interior administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min summoned him to the secretariat, but Emperor Yuan kept him south to serve as interior administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 臨行，帝為置酒，謂曰：「今之會稽，昔之關中，足食足兵，在於良守。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure the emperor set wine for him and said, "Today's Kuaiji is yesterday's Guanzhong—ample food and ample arms lie in having a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor said, "Kuaiji is now what Guanzhong once was—plenty of grain and troops if the governor is right."

sentences.zh: 以君有蒞任之方，是以相屈。

translations.literal: Because you have the method of taking office, therefore we bend you to it."
translations.idiomatic: You have a proven hand at administration, which is why we ask this of you."

sentences.zh: 四方分崩，當匡振圮運。

translations.literal: The four quarters split and crumble; you ought to rescue and brace the tottering fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is shattered; we need you to shore up what remains."

sentences.zh: 政之所先，君為言之。

translations.literal: Of what policy ought to take precedence, you speak it."
translations.idiomatic: Tell me which policies must come first."

sentences.zh: 」恢陳謝，因對曰：「今天下喪亂，風俗陵遲，宜尊五美，屏四惡，進忠實，退浮華。

translations.literal: Hui expressed thanks and thereupon replied, saying, "Now the realm is ruined and customs have slid; one ought to honor the five beauties, banish the four evils, advance the loyal and solid, and retire the flashy and hollow."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui thanked him and answered: "In these ruined times we must honor the five virtues, cast out the four vices, promote honest men, and dismiss empty show."

sentences.zh: 」帝深納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 太興初，以政績第一，詔曰：「自頃多難，官長數易，益有諸弊，雖聖人猶久于其道，然後化成，況其餘乎！

translations.literal: At the start of Taixing, because his administrative merit ranked first, an edict said, "Since recently there have been many hardships, magistrates have repeatedly changed, increasing every kind of abuse—even sages need long practice in their way before transformation is complete, how much more the rest!
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixing, citing Zhuge Hui's top-ranked administration, the court observed that frequent turnover of magistrates had bred abuse—even sages need time to teach customs.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝稱'與我共安天下者，其惟良二千石'，斯言信矣。

translations.literal: Han Emperor Xuan said, 'Those who with me together pacify the empire are surely the good two-thousand-bushels'—that saying is true.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xuandi's line about good "two-thousand-bushel" governors still holds true.

sentences.zh: 是以黃霸等或十年，或二十年而不徙，所以能濟其中興之勳也。

translations.literal: Therefore Huang Ba and the like, some ten years, some twenty years without transfer, thereby were able to complete the merit of their restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Huang Ba held the same post ten or twenty years and so could finish the work of revival.

sentences.zh: 賞罰黜陟，所以明政道也。

translations.literal: Rewards, punishments, dismissals, and promotions are the means to clarify the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Clear rewards and promotions are how government shows its course.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史諸葛恢蒞官三年，政清人和，為諸郡首，宜進其位班，以勸風教。

translations.literal: Interior Administrator of Kuaiji Zhuge Hui has held office three years; his government is pure and the people harmonious; he heads the commanderies—ought to advance his rank and grade so as to encourage customs and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui has governed Kuaiji three years with clean rule and popular harmony; he leads every commandery and deserves a raise to model others.

sentences.zh: 今增恢秩中二千石。」

translations.literal: Now increase Hui's salary to the fully two-thousand-bushel grade."
translations.idiomatic: His stipend is raised to the full two-thousand-bushel rank."

sentences.zh: 頃之，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: Shortly he left office for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜中書令。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed supervisor of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he became supervisor of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王敦上恢為丹陽尹，以久疾免。

translations.literal: Wang Dun nominated Hui as intendant of Danyang; because of long illness he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun named him intendant of Danyang, but chronic illness forced him out.

sentences.zh: 明帝征敦，以恢為侍中，加奉車都尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming campaigned against Dun, he appointed Hui attendant-in-ordinary with the added title colonel who follows the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming made him attendant-in-ordinary with colonel who follows the carriage for the campaign against Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 討王含有功，進封建安伯，以先爵賜次子虪為關內侯。

translations.literal: For merit in punishing Wang Han he was advanced in enfeoffment to earl of Jian'an, and with his former noble title enfeoffed his second son Shu as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: For crushing Wang Han's revolt he was raised to earl of Jian'an and passed his old title to his second son Zhuge Shu as marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 又拜恢後將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: Again Hui was appointed general of the rear and interior administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named general of the rear and interior administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中，遷左民尚書、武陵王師、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, moved to minister of the left people, tutor to the prince of Wuling, minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as attendant-in-ordinary, he became minister for the common people, tutor to the prince of Wuling, and minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍、銀青光祿大夫、領選本州大中正、尚書令，常侍、吏部如故。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted right vice director of the secretariat, with the added titles cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, grand household silver and blue, concurrent selector as senior rectifier of his home province, grand director of the secretariat; attendant-in-ordinary and ministry of personnel as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice director, then grand director, with cavalier attendant, silver-and-blue grand household, home-province senior rectifier, while keeping personnel duties.

sentences.zh: 成帝踐阼，加侍中、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he was given attendant-in-ordinary and grand household gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng he received gold-and-purple grand household with attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈左光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded left grand household and ceremonial parity with the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors included left grand household and three-excellency ceremonial rank.

sentences.zh: 賵贈之禮，一依太尉興平伯故事，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: The gifts for obsequies followed in every case the precedent of Grand Commandant village earl of Xingping; his posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral rites matched those for the village earl of Xingping; his epithet was Jing, "Reverent."

sentences.zh: 祠乙太牢。

translations.literal: Sacrifice used the ta lao victim grade.
translations.idiomatic: He received burial sacrifice of the highest ox-offering grade.

sentences.zh: 子甝嗣，位至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Chan succeeded him; his office reached cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuge Chan inherited the line and rose to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 恢兄頤，字道回，亦為元帝所器重，終於太常。

translations.literal: Hui's elder brother Yi, courtesy Daohui, was also prized by Emperor Yuan and ended as grand astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhuge Yi, courtesy Daohui, likewise won Emperor Yuan's favor and died as grand astrologer.

sentences.zh: 殷浩，字深源，陳郡長平人也。

translations.literal: Yin Hao, courtesy Shenyuan, was a man of Changping in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, courtesy Shenyuan, came from Changping in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 父羨，字洪喬，為豫章太守，都下人士因其致書者百餘函，行次石頭，皆投之水中，曰：「沈者自沈，浮者自浮，殷洪喬不為致書郵。

translations.literal: His father Xian, courtesy Hongqiao, was administrator of Yuzhang; more than a hundred letters from capital gentlemen were entrusted to him to deliver; halting at Stone he threw them all into the water, saying, "What sinks sinks, what floats floats—Yin Hongqiao does not serve as postman for letters."
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin Xian, as Yuzhang prefect, once dumped a hundred letters from Luoyang dignitaries into the Yangzi at Stone, saying, "Sink or swim—I am no mail courier."

sentences.zh: 」其資性介立如此。

translations.literal: His inborn nature was upright and detached to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his stubborn integrity.

sentences.zh: 終於光祿勳。

translations.literal: He ended as chamberlain for the palace revenues.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as chamberlain for the palace revenues.

sentences.zh: 浩識度清遠，弱冠有美名，尤善玄言，與叔父融俱好《老》《易》。

translations.literal: Hao's insight and bearing were clear and far-reaching; while still weak-capped he had a fine reputation; he was especially good at arcane discourse, together with his uncle Rong both loving the Laozi and Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao was celebrated for subtle learning and lofty manner; with his uncle Yin Rong he mastered Daoist exegesis of the Laozi and Zhouyi.

sentences.zh: 融與浩口談則辭屈，著篇則融勝，浩由是為風流談論者所宗。

translations.literal: When Rong and Hao debated orally Rong's words bent; when they wrote treatises Rong prevailed; Hao for this reason became the patriarch whom the refined debaters honored.
translations.idiomatic: In talk Yin Rong could corner him, but on paper Yin Hao won the day—so the salon set Yin Hao at its head.

sentences.zh: 或問浩曰：「將蒞官而夢棺，將得財而夢糞，何也？

translations.literal: Someone asked Hao, saying, "About to take office yet dreaming of a coffin, about to obtain wealth yet dreaming of dung—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked why dreaming of coffers meant promotion and dung meant money.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「官本臭腐，故將得官而夢屍，錢本糞土，故將得錢而夢穢。

translations.literal: Hao said, "Office fundamentally is stench and rot; therefore about to obtain office one dreams of corpses; money fundamentally is muck and soil; therefore about to obtain money one dreams of filth."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao answered, "Rank smells of carrion—hence corpse dreams; cash is filth—hence dung dreams."

sentences.zh: 」時人以為名言。

translations.literal: Men of the time took this for a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: Wits hailed the reply as a classic line.

sentences.zh: 三府辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: The three offices summoned him; all he declined.
translations.idiomatic: The three highest bureaus called him; he refused each.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍庾亮引為記室參軍，累遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the West Yu Liang brought him in as recorder-in-chief adjutant; by stages he was promoted chief clerk to the minister of education on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang made him recording adjutant; he rose to left chief clerk under the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 安西庾翼復請為司馬。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the West Yu Yi again requested him as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi again asked him to serve as marshal.

sentences.zh: 除侍中、安西軍司，並稱疾不起。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant-in-ordinary and marshal of the army who guards the west, both of which he claimed illness and did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: He was named attendant-in-ordinary and western-army marshal but pleaded sick and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 遂屏居墓所，幾將十年，于時擬之管、葛。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lived in seclusion at the tomb site, nearly ten years; at the time they compared him to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: For almost a decade he lived as a recluse at his father's tomb while rumor compared him to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 王蒙、謝尚猶伺其出處，以卜江左興亡，因相與省之，知浩有確然之志。

translations.literal: Wang Meng and Xie Shang still watched his coming forth or staying put to divine whether the left of the Yangzi would rise or fall; therefore together they visited him and learned that Hao had a firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng and Xie Shang watched whether he would emerge, taking it as an omen for the southland, and a visit showed Yin Hao would not budge.

sentences.zh: 既反，相謂曰：「深源不起，當如蒼生何！

translations.literal: When they returned they said to each other, "If Shenyuan does not rise, what will become of the common folk!"
translations.idiomatic: Leaving, they said, "If Yin Hao stays hidden, what becomes of the people?"

sentences.zh: 」庾翼貽浩書曰：「當今江東社稷安危，內委何、褚諸君，外托庾、桓數族，恐不得百年無憂，亦朝夕而弊。

translations.literal: Yu Yi sent Hao a letter, saying, "Now the altars east of the Yangzi, their safety and danger, within are entrusted to the gentlemen He, Chu, and the rest; without are entrusted to the several clans Yu and Huan—your servant fears one cannot be without worry for a hundred years, but also morning and evening decay.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi wrote urging him: the realm's fate rested on inner ministers and outer generals, and could not survive long without Yin Hao.

sentences.zh: 足下少標令名，十餘年間，位經內外，而欲潛居利貞，斯理難全。

translations.literal: You from youth have borne a fair name; in more than ten years your posts have passed through inner and outer, yet you wish to hide and preserve profit and constancy—this principle is hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao had held high office yet clung to reclusion—Yu Yi called that stance untenable.

sentences.zh: 且夫濟一時之務，須一時之勝，何必德均古人，韻齊先達邪！

translations.literal: Moreover to aid the tasks of a moment requires the excellence of a moment—why must virtue match the ancients and tone match the former worthies!"
translations.idiomatic: A crisis needs timely talent, not a perfect sage."

sentences.zh: 王夷甫，先朝風流士也，然吾薄其立名非真，而始終莫取。

translations.literal: Wang Yanxi was a refined gentleman of the former court, yet your servant despises him for establishing a name not genuine, and from first to last your servant does not take him.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed Wang Yan as a hollow poseur.

sentences.zh: 若以道非虞夏，自當超然獨往，而不能謀始，大合聲譽，極致名位，正當抑揚名教，以靜亂源。

translations.literal: If because the Way is not that of Yu and Xia he ought naturally to have gone alone aloft, yet he could not plan the beginning, greatly joined reputation and sound, reached the utmost in name and rank—he ought to have raised and lowered the teachings of names to still the sources of chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Had Wang Yan truly scorned worldly rank he should have lived the recluse's life; instead he chased fame yet preached Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 而乃高談《莊》《老》，說空終日，雖云談道，實長華競。

translations.literal: Yet he discoursed high on Zhuang and Laozi, speaking emptiness all day—though he called it discussing the Way, in reality he lengthened vain rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: His all-day "dark learning" only fed empty competition.

sentences.zh: 及其末年，人望猶存，思安懼亂，寄命推務。

translations.literal: When he reached his late years men's expectation still existed; he thought of safety and feared chaos and entrusted his fate to pushing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he clung to office while preaching detachment.

sentences.zh: 而甫自申述，徇小好名，既身囚胡虜，棄言非所。

translations.literal: Yet Yan himself expounded, pursuing petty fondness for name; in the end his body was imprisoned by Hu captives, casting aside speech not where it belonged.
translations.idiomatic: He ended a barbarian captive—irony complete.

sentences.zh: 凡明德君子，遇會處際，寧可然乎？

translations.literal: As a rule, when enlightened virtuous gentlemen meet occasions and situations, can it be thus?
translations.idiomatic: Can worthy men behave that way?

sentences.zh: 而世皆然之。

translations.literal: Yet the age all deemed it right.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the world called Wang Yan right.

sentences.zh: 益知名實之未定，弊風之未革也。

translations.literal: This increases knowledge that name and reality are not yet settled and that corrupt custom is not yet reformed.
translations.idiomatic: That shows how hollow fashion still was.

sentences.zh: 」浩固辭不起。

translations.literal: Hao firmly declined and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao still refused office.

sentences.zh: 建元初，庾冰兄弟及何充等相繼卒。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jianyuan era Yu Bing's brothers and He Chong and others died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyuan the Yu brothers and He Chong died in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝時在籓，始綜萬幾，衛將軍褚裒薦浩，徵為建武將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen at the time was still in his princedom and first took charge of myriad handles; General Who Guards the Guard Chu Pou recommended Hao; he was summoned as general who establishes might and inspector of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: While still prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu took power; Chu Pou recommended Yin Hao as general who establishes might and governor of Yang.

sentences.zh: 浩上疏陳讓，並致箋于簡文，具自申敘。

translations.literal: Hao submitted a memorial stating decline and also sent a note to Jianwen, fully stating himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao memorialized his refusal and wrote Sima Yu privately to explain.

sentences.zh: 簡文答之曰：「屬當厄運，危弊理盡。

translations.literal: Jianwen answered him, saying, "We belong to a fated misfortune; peril and decay are at the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu answered that the dynasty faced ruin.

sentences.zh: 誠賴時有其才，不復遠求版築。

translations.literal: Truly we rely on the age having its talent; we do not again seek far for Fu Yue from the plasterer's wall.
translations.idiomatic: The throne needs able men now, not mythical hermits.

sentences.zh: 足下沈識淹長，思綜通練，起而明之，足以經濟。

translations.literal: You sink in insight and are deep and long; your thought is comprehensive and practiced; rising to clarify it suffices to order and aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao's breadth of mind could save the state.

sentences.zh: 若復深存挹退，苟遂本懷，吾恐天下之事於此去矣，今紘領不振，晉網不綱，願蹈東海，復可得邪！

translations.literal: If again you deeply preserve yielding retreat and heedlessly follow your original intent, your servant fears the affairs of the realm from this will go; now the leading thread is not stretched and Jin's net is not corded—your servant wishes to tread the eastern sea—can it again be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: If you cling to reclusion, the dynasty unravels—Sima Yu said he would sooner drown than watch Yin Hao stay home."

sentences.zh: 由此言之，足下去就即是時之廢興，時之廢興則家國不異。

translations.literal: From this speaking, your going or staying is precisely the age's ruin or rise; the age's ruin or rise then differs not from house and state.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao's choice was the dynasty's life or death.

sentences.zh: 足下弘思之，靜算之，亦將有以深鑒可否。

translations.literal: You enlarge your thought and quietly calculate—thereby you will also have means deeply to examine what may or may not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He begged Yin Hao to weigh duty soberly.

sentences.zh: 望必廢本懷，率群情也。

translations.literal: Your hope must set aside original intent and follow the multitude's feeling."
translations.idiomatic: He asked Yin Hao to heed public expectation."

sentences.zh: 」浩頻陳讓，自三月至七月，乃受拜焉。

translations.literal: Hao repeatedly stated decline from the third month to the seventh month, then accepted the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao refused from spring to midsummer, then took office.

sentences.zh: 時桓溫既滅蜀，威勢轉振，朝廷憚之。

translations.literal: At the time Huan Wen had already extinguished Shu and his awe-inspiring momentum turned ever stronger; the court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's conquest of Shu had made him terrifying to the court.

sentences.zh: 簡文以浩有盛名，朝野推伏，故引為心膂，以抗于溫，於是與溫頗相疑貳。

translations.literal: Jianwen because Hao had a great name, court and countryside pushed and submitted to him, therefore brought him in as heart and backbone to oppose Wen; thereupon with Wen he was rather mutually suspicious and divided.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu promoted Yin Hao to counterbalance Huan Wen, sowing mutual distrust.

sentences.zh: 會遭父憂，去職，時以蔡謨攝揚州，以俟浩，服闋，徵為尚書僕射，不拜。

translations.literal: As it happened he encountered mourning for his father and left office; at the time because Cai Mo acted for Yang province to await Hao, when mourning ended he was summoned vice director of the secretariat; he did not accept the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, Cai Mo held Yang province in his stead; after mourning Yin Hao was offered vice director of the secretariat but declined.

sentences.zh: 復為建武將軍、揚州刺史，遂參綜朝權。

translations.literal: Again he was general who establishes might and inspector of Yang province, thereupon joining in comprehensive oversight of court power.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named general who establishes might and governor of Yang, then entered central policy-making.

sentences.zh: 潁川荀羨少有令聞，浩擢為義興、吳郡，以為羽翼。

translations.literal: Yingchuan Xun Xian in youth had a fair reputation; Hao promoted him to Yixing and Wu commanderies as wings.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted the talented Xun Xian to Yixing and Wu as allies.

sentences.zh: 王羲之密說浩、羨，令與桓溫和同，不宜內構嫌隙，浩不從。

translations.literal: Wang Xizhi secretly urged Hao and Xian to harmonize with Huan Wen and ought not inwardly construct suspicion and rift; Hao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi privately begged Yin Hao and Xun Xian to work with Huan Wen; Yin Hao refused.

sentences.zh: 及石季龍死，胡中大亂，朝過欲遂蕩平關河，於是以浩為中軍將軍、假節、都督揚豫徐兗青五州軍事。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong died, the Hu within were greatly in turmoil; the court wished then to sweep clear Guan and the Yellow River; therefore Hao was made general of the central army, with credential staff, area commander for military affairs in Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, and Qing five provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's death sparked northern chaos; the court named Yin Hao general of the central army with command over five provinces to recover the heartland.

sentences.zh: 浩既受命，以中原為己任，上疏北征許洛。

translations.literal: Hao having received the charge took the Central Plain as his own responsibility and submitted a memorial for northern expedition to Xu and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao vowed to reclaim the Central Plain and memorialized a drive on Xu and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 將發，墜馬，時咸惡之。

translations.literal: About to set out he fell from a horse; at the time all considered it ominous.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure he fell from his horse—a bad omen everyone noted.

sentences.zh: 既而以淮南太守陳逵、兗州刺史蔡裔為前鋒，安西將軍謝尚、北中郎將荀羨為督統，開江西田千餘頃，以為軍儲。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Administrator of Huainan Chen Kui and inspector of Yan province Cai Yi as van, General Who Guards the West Xie Shang and North General of the Gentlemen Xun Xian as overseers, he opened fields on the west of the river more than a thousand qing to serve as army stores.
translations.idiomatic: He named Chen Kui and Cai Yi vanguard commanders, Xie Shang and Xun Xian as coordinators, and opened a thousand qing of farmland west of the river for grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 師次壽陽，潛誘苻健大臣梁安、雷弱兒等，使殺健，許以關右之任。

translations.literal: The army halted at Shouyang; secretly he enticed Fu Jian's great ministers Liang An and Lei Ruo'er and others to kill Jian, promising them office west of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouyang he bribed Fu Jian's ministers Liang An and Lei Ruo'er to murder their sovereign with promises of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 初，降人魏脫卒，其弟憬代領部曲。

translations.literal: At first surrendered man Wei Tuo died; his younger brother Jing succeeded in leading the following.
translations.idiomatic: The defector Wei Tuo had died; his brother Wei Jing led his followers.

sentences.zh: 姚襄殺憬，以並其眾，浩大惡之，使龍驤將軍劉啟守譙，遷襄于梁。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang killed Jing in order to annex his host; Hao greatly hated this and sent General Who Prances the Dragon Liu Qi to guard Qiao, moving Xiang to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang murdered Wei Jing and absorbed his troops; Yin Hao detested this, posted Liu Qi at Qiao, and shifted Yao Xiang to Liang.

sentences.zh: 既而魏氏子弟往來壽陽，襄益猜懼。

translations.literal: Afterward Wei clan younger kin came and went at Shouyang; Xiang grew ever more suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Wei clansmen then shuttled through Shouyang, stoking Yao Xiang's fears.

sentences.zh: 俄而襄部曲有欲歸浩者，襄殺之，浩於是謀誅襄。

translations.literal: Shortly there were in Xiang's following some who wished to return to Hao; Xiang killed them; Hao thereupon plotted to execute Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xiang executed men who wanted to defect to Yin Hao, Yin Hao resolved to kill him.

sentences.zh: 會苻健殺其大臣，健兄子眉自洛陽西奔，浩以為梁安事捷，意苻健已死，請進屯洛陽，修復園陵，使襄為前驅，冠軍將軍劉洽鎮鹿台，建武將軍劉遁據倉垣，又求解揚州，專鎮洛陽，詔不許。

translations.literal: As it happened Fu Jian killed his great ministers; Jian's elder brother's son Mei fled west from Luoyang; Hao thought Liang An's affair had succeeded, supposed Fu Jian already dead, requested to advance and garrison Luoyang, repair the imperial parks and tombs, made Xiang vanguard, General Who Champions the Army Liu Zhi guarded Deer Terrace, General Who Establishes Might Liu Dun held Cangyuan, again requested to relinquish Yang province and solely garrison Luoyang; the edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian slaughtered his ministers while his nephew Fu Mei bolted west from Luoyang, Yin Hao mistook a coup rumor for Fu Jian's death, sought to occupy Luoyang and restore the tombs, sent Yao Xiang ahead, posted Liu Zhi at Deer Terrace and Liu Dun at Cangyuan, and again asked to shed Yang province for a Luoyang-only command—the court refused.

sentences.zh: 浩既至許昌，會張遇反，謝尚又敗績，浩還壽陽。

translations.literal: When Hao had reached Xuchang, as it happened Zhang Yu rebelled, Xie Shang again was defeated, and Hao returned to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuchang Zhang Yu mutinied, Xie Shang lost a battle, and Yin Hao fell back to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 後復進軍，次山桑，而襄反，浩懼，棄輜重退保譙城，器械軍儲皆為襄所掠，士卒多亡叛。

translations.literal: Later again he advanced the army, halted at Shansang, but Xiang rebelled; Hao feared, abandoned baggage trains and withdrew to guard Qiao city; weapons and army stores were all plundered by Xiang, and soldiers for the most part fled or rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced again to Shansang, but Yao Xiang rose against him; Yin Hao fled to Qiao, losing supplies and most of his army.

sentences.zh: 浩遣劉啟、王彬之擊襄于山桑，並為襄所殺。

translations.literal: Hao dispatched Liu Qi and Wang Binzhi to strike Xiang at Shansang; both were killed by Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi and Wang Binzhi died fighting Yao Xiang at Shansang.

sentences.zh: 桓溫素忌浩，及聞其敗，上疏罪浩曰：

translations.literal: Huan Wen from of old envied Hao; when he heard of his defeat he submitted a memorial blaming Hao, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, long jealous, seized the defeat to memorialize:

sentences.zh: 案中軍將軍浩過蒙朝恩，叨竊非據，寵靈超卓，再司京輦，不能恭慎所任，恪居職次，而侵官離局，高下在心。

translations.literal: Your servant investigates: General of the central army Hao has excessively received court favor, improperly occupied a post beyond his station, favor and numinous grace superlative, twice presiding over the capital precincts; he could not respectfully be careful in what he was entrusted, scrupulously occupy his office rank, but encroached on offices and departed from his bureau, high and low according to his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He accused Yin Hao of arrogating power, bungling two capital commands, and ignoring duty.

sentences.zh: 前司徒臣謨執義履素，位居台輔，師傅先帝，朝之元老，年登七十，以禮請退，雖臨軒固辭，不順恩旨，適足以明遜讓之風，弘優賢之禮。

translations.literal: Former Minister of Education your servant Mo upheld righteousness and trod plainness, his position reaching ministerial summit, tutor to former emperors, court elder, his years climbing seventy, by ritual requesting retirement—though facing the hall he firmly declined, not following favor's intent—this sufficed only to clarify the wind of yielding and retiring, to magnify the rite that favors worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Cai Mo's stubborn refusal of high office as true modesty.

sentences.zh: 而浩虛生狡說，疑誤朝聽，獄之有司，將致大辟。

translations.literal: Yet Hao vainly produced crafty explanations, doubted and misled court hearing, and would hand him to the offices, about to bring on the great execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao had slandered Cai Mo to the point of capital charges.

sentences.zh: 自羯胡夭亡，群凶殄滅，而百姓塗炭，企遲拯接。

translations.literal: Since the Jie Hu perished young and the flock of villains was extinguished, yet the hundred surnames are smeared in mud and charcoal, standing on tiptoe awaiting rescue and support.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Hu gone the people still suffered, awaiting rescue.

sentences.zh: 浩受專征之重，無雪恥之志，坐自封植，妄生風塵，遂使寇仇稽誅，奸逆並起，華夏鼎沸，黎元殄悴。

translations.literal: Hao received the weight of sole expedition yet had no will to wash shame; sitting he sealed and planted himself, wantonly raising dust and wind, thereupon causing the foe and enemy to delay execution, treacherous rebels together rising, Huaxia boiling like a cauldron, black-haired folk utterly withered.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao squandered his mandate, let rebels multiply, and left the heartland in flames.

sentences.zh: 浩懼罪將及，不容於朝，外聲進討，內求苟免。

translations.literal: Hao feared punishment would reach him and he would not be tolerated at court; outwardly he proclaimed advance to punish, inwardly he sought to escape by luck.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing impeachment, Yin Hao talked of new offensives while angling for personal escape.

sentences.zh: 出次壽陽，頓甲彌年，傾天府之資，竭五州之力，收合無賴，以自強衛，爵命無章，猜害罔顧。

translations.literal: He went out and halted at Shouyang, halted armor a full year, tipped the celestial treasury's resources, exhausted the five provinces' strength, gathered and joined worthless men to strengthen his personal guard, noble orders were without pattern, suspicion and harm were unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: He camped a year at Shouyang, draining the treasury and five provinces to hire riffraff as bodyguards while handing out rank without rule.

sentences.zh: 故范豐之屬反叛於芍陂，奇德、龍會作變於肘腋。

translations.literal: Therefore Fan Feng's sort rebelled at Shaobei; Qi De and Long Hui made mutiny in the elbow and armpit.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Feng mutinied at Shaobei; Qi De and Long Hui struck from within his own camp.

sentences.zh: 羌帥姚襄率眾歸化，遣其母弟入質京邑，浩不能撫而用之，陰圖殺害，再遣剌客，為襄所覺。

translations.literal: Qiang commander Yao Xiang led the host to submit to transformation, sending his younger brother by the same mother as hostage in the capital; Hao could not cherish and use him but secretly plotted killing, twice dispatching assassins; Xiang perceived it.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang had pledged loyalty and sent kin as hostages; Yin Hao tried twice to murder him instead.

sentences.zh: 襄遂惶懼，用致逆命。

translations.literal: Xiang thereupon was frightened and fearful, thereby bringing on rebellious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang turned rebel out of fear.

sentences.zh: 生長亂階，自浩始也。

translations.literal: Growing the steps of chaos began from Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The spiral of rebellion began with Yin Hao.

sentences.zh: 復不能以時掃滅，縱放小豎，鼓行毒害，身狼狽于山桑，軍破碎于梁國，舟車焚燒，輜重覆沒。

translations.literal: Again he could not in due time sweep and destroy them, but released and let go the petty brats, who beat drums and marched spreading poison; his person was in straits at Shansang, his army shattered in Liang commandery, boats and carts burned, baggage trains overturned and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to crush them in time, let minor foes roam free, and was routed at Shansang and in Liang, losing wagons and stores.

sentences.zh: 三軍積實，反以資寇，精甲利器，更為賊用。

translations.literal: The three armies' accumulated stores instead thereby supplied the bandits; fine armor and sharp weapons further became tools for the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His supplies armed the enemy; his armor re-equipped them.

sentences.zh: 神怒人怨，眾之所棄，傾危之憂，將及社稷。

translations.literal: Spirits angry and men resentful, abandoned by the multitude, the worry of toppling peril will reach the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men turned on him, endangering the altars themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣所以忘寢屏營，啟處無地。

translations.literal: This is why your servant forgets sleep and is restless, having nowhere to stand or sit.
translations.idiomatic: Hence your memorialist cannot sleep.

sentences.zh: 夫率正顯義，所以致訓，明罰敕法，所以齊眾，伏願陛下上追唐堯放命之刑下鑒《春秋》無君之典。

translations.literal: Now leading the upright and displaying righteousness is the means to convey instruction; clarifying punishments and ordering law is the means to align the multitude; prostrate, I wish Your Majesty above pursue Tang Yao's punishment for those who defy orders, below take mirror from the Spring and Autumn canon on lordlessness.
translations.idiomatic: He begged the emperor to punish Yin Hao as Yao punished rebels and the Chunqiu punished traitors.

sentences.zh: 若聖上含弘，末忍誅殛，且宜遐棄，擯之荒裔。

translations.literal: If the sage sovereign is inclusive and tolerant and has not yet the heart to execute, then at least he ought to be cast far away, banished to the wild border.
translations.idiomatic: If execution is too harsh, at least exile him beyond the pale.

sentences.zh: 雖未足以塞山海之責，粗可以宣誡於將來矣。

translations.literal: Though not sufficient to plug the blame of mountain and sea, roughly it can proclaim warning to those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: Even exile would warn posterity.

sentences.zh: 竟坐廢為庶人，徙于東陽之信安縣。

translations.literal: In the end he was judged and dismissed to commoner status and banished to Xinan county in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao was reduced to commoner and banished to Xinan in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 浩少與溫齊名，而每心競。

translations.literal: Hao from youth was paired in fame with Wen, yet always competed in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao had rivaled Huan Wen in reputation since youth.

sentences.zh: 溫嘗問浩：「君何如我？

translations.literal: Wen once asked Hao, "How do you compare to me?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen once asked how Yin Hao rated against himself.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「我與君周旋久，寧作我也。

translations.literal: Hao said, "I and you have circled long together—I would still just be myself."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao answered, "We have known each other too long for me to be anyone but myself."

sentences.zh: 」溫既以雄豪自許，每輕浩，浩不之憚也。

translations.literal: Wen since by heroic boldness prided himself, always belittled Hao; Hao did not fear him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen swaggered as a hero and sneered at Yin Hao, who did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 至是，溫語人曰：「少時吾與浩共騎竹馬，我棄去，浩輒取之，故當出我下也。

translations.literal: At this Wen told people, "In youth I with Hao together rode bamboo horses; I cast mine away and Hao always picked it up—so he ought to rank below me."
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat Huan Wen sneered that even as boys Yin Hao had always picked up his cast-off toys—proof Yin Hao was always second best.

sentences.zh: 」又謂郗超曰：「浩有德有言，向使作令僕，足以儀刑百揆，朝廷用違其才耳。」

translations.literal: Again he said to Xi Chao, "Hao has virtue and speech; had he been made minister or vice director, he would have been enough to model the hundred handles; the court used him contrary to his talent."
translations.idiomatic: To Xi Chao he granted Yin Hao's gifts but said civil office would have suited him better.

sentences.zh: 浩雖被黜放，口無怨言，夷神委命，談詠不輟，雖家人不見其有流放之戚。

translations.literal: Though Hao was dismissed and banished, in speech he had no resentful words; spirit calm he entrusted fate, discoursing and chanting without stop; even family members did not see him show the sorrow of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Banished, Yin Hao showed no bitterness to his household.

sentences.zh: 但終日書空，作「咄咄怪事」四字而已。

translations.literal: Only all day he traced characters in the air, making merely the four words 'Strange business indeed, tut tut.'
translations.idiomatic: All day he traced "What a strange business" in empty air.

sentences.zh: 浩甥韓伯，浩素賞愛之，隨至徙所，經歲還都，浩送至渚側，詠曹顏遠詩云：「富貴他人合，貧賤親戚離。

translations.literal: Hao's sister's son Han Bo, whom Hao always prized and loved, followed to the place of banishment; after a year returning to the capital, Hao saw him off beside the islet, chanting Cao Yanyuan's poem, saying, "Wealth joins with others; poverty and lowliness part kin."
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Han Bo accompanied him into exile; on Han's return Yin Hao quoted Cao's verse on how fortune divides friends.

sentences.zh: 」因而泣下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept.
translations.idiomatic: He wept at the parting.

sentences.zh: 後溫將以浩為尚書令，遺書告之，浩欣然許焉。

translations.literal: Later Wen was about to appoint Hao grand director of the secretariat and sent a letter informing him; Hao gladly promised.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huan Wen offered him grand director of the secretariat; Yin Hao eagerly accepted.

sentences.zh: 將答書，慮有謬誤，開閉者數十，竟達空函，大忤溫意，由是遂絕。

translations.literal: About to answer the letter, fearing mistakes, he opened and closed it several tens of times, yet in the end delivered an empty box, greatly offending Wen's intent; on this account relations then broke off.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed and reopened his reply so many times he sent an empty envelope—Huan Wen never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 永和十二年卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yonghe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 356.

sentences.zh: 子涓，亦有美名，咸安初，桓溫廢太宰、武陵王晞，誣涓及庾倩與晞謀反，害之。

translations.literal: His son Juan also had a fair name; at the start of Xian'an, Huan Wen deposed grand tutor and prince of Wuling Xi, falsely accusing Juan and Yu Qian of plotting rebellion with Xi, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin Juan was murdered in 371 when Huan Wen framed him with Prince Xi and Yu Qian.

sentences.zh: 浩後將改葬，其故吏顧悅之上疏訟浩曰：

translations.literal: Later when Hao was about to be reburied, his former subordinate Gu Yuezhi submitted a memorial pleading Hao's case, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Hao was reinterred, Gu Yuezhi memorialized in his defense:

sentences.zh: 伏見故中軍將軍、揚州刺史殷浩體德沈粹，識理淹長，風流雅勝，聲蓋當時，再臨神州，萬里肅清，勳績茂著，聖朝欽嘉，遂授分陝推轂之任。

translations.literal: Prostrate I have seen that former General of the central army and Inspector of Yang province Yin Hao embodied virtue deep and pure, grasped principle broad and long, refined bearing excelled, his fame covered the age; twice he faced the divine region and within ten thousand li brought pure quiet, merit and achievement luxuriantly manifest; the sagely court admired him and therefore gave him the duty of dividing Shaan and pushing the chariot shaft.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial praised Yin Hao's past virtue and northern command.

sentences.zh: 戎旗既建，出鎮壽陽，驅其豺狼，翦其荊棘，收羅向義，廣開屯田，沐雨櫛風，等勤台僕。

translations.literal: Military banners already raised, he went out to hold Shouyang, drove their wolves and jackals, cut their brambles and thorns, gathered those who turned to righteousness, broadly opened tuntian fields, bathed in rain and combed wind, toiling equal to ministers of state.
translations.idiomatic: It lauded his garrison work and colonization at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 仰憑皇威，群醜革面，進軍河洛，修復園陵。

translations.literal: Looking up relying on imperial majesty, the flock of villains changed face; he advanced the army to the Yellow River and Luoyang and repaired the imperial parks and tombs.
translations.idiomatic: It credited his plan to restore the Luoyang tombs.

sentences.zh: 不虞之變，中路猖蹶，遂令為山之功崩于垂成，忠款之志於是而廢。

translations.literal: Unexpected change midway brought wild collapse, thereupon making the merit that was mountain-high crumble at the verge of completion, the intent of loyal sincerity from this was cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Misfortune wrecked his campaign at the last moment.

sentences.zh: 既受削黜，自擯山海，杜門終身，與世兩絕，可謂克己復禮，窮而無怨者也。

translations.literal: Having received dismissal and demotion, he banished himself among mountain and sea, shut his gate to the end of his life, severed from the age on both sides—this can be called restraining self and returning to ritual, in extremity yet without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: It argued that exile had made Yin Hao a model of patient resignation.

sentences.zh: 尋浩所犯，蓋負敗之常科，非即情之永責。

translations.literal: Examining Hao's offense, it is covered by the ordinary statute for defeat, not the everlasting blame of passion.
translations.idiomatic: His faults were those of any defeated general.

sentences.zh: 論其名德深誠則如彼，察其補過罪己則如此，豈可棄而不恤，使法有餘冤！

translations.literal: Discussing his name and virtue so deep and sincere as that, examining his mending faults and blaming himself as this—how can one cast aside and not pity, letting the law retain surplus injustice!
translations.idiomatic: Justice should not leave him unrehabilitated.

sentences.zh: 方今宅兆已成。

translations.literal: Now the tomb precinct is already completed.
translations.idiomatic: His tomb is ready.

sentences.zh: 埏隧已開，懸棺而窆，禮同庶人，存亡有非命之分，九泉無自訴之斯，仰感三良，昊天罔極。

translations.literal: The tunnel is already opened; suspending the coffin and lowering it, the rites match commoners; between life and death there is a share not of fate; in the nine springs there is no self to plead—looking up I feel for the three good men, vast Heaven has no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Burial as a commoner shames a man of his stature.

sentences.zh: 若使明詔爰發，旌我善人，崇復本官，遠彰幽昧，斯則國家威恩有兼濟之美，死而可作，無負心之恨。

translations.literal: If a clear edict then issues, hoisting my good man, restoring his original office and distantly manifesting the hidden and dim, then the state's awesome favor will have the beauty of aiding both; if dead he could rise, he would have no regret of betrayed heart.
translations.idiomatic: Restoring his post would honor living and dead alike.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，詔追復浩本官。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, an edict posthumously restored Hao's original office.
translations.idiomatic: The throne restored Yin Hao's former titles.

sentences.zh: 顧悅之

translations.literal: Gu Yuezhi
translations.idiomatic: The text next treats Gu Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 顧悅之，字君叔，少有義行。

translations.literal: Gu Yuezhi, courtesy Junshu, from youth had righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yuezhi, courtesy Junshu, was known early for principled conduct.

sentences.zh: 與簡文同年，而髮早白。

translations.literal: He was the same age as Jianwen, yet his hair whitened early.
translations.idiomatic: He was Emperor Jianwen's age-mate but grayed young.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「松柏之姿，經霜猶茂；

translations.literal: He replied, saying, "The posture of pine and cypress, through frost still flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Pine and cypress stay green through frost;

sentences.zh: 蒲柳常質，望秋先零。

translations.literal: the nature of rush and willow, gazing toward autumn first withers."
translations.idiomatic: willow and rush wither at the first hint of autumn."

sentences.zh: 」簡文悅其對。

translations.literal: Jianwen was pleased with his answer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen delighted in the reply.

sentences.zh: 始將抗表訟浩，浩親故多謂非宜，悅之決意以聞，又與朝臣爭論，故眾無以奪焉。

translations.literal: When he first was about to submit a memorial pleading Hao's case, Hao's kin and old friends mostly said it was not fitting; Yuezhi resolved to make it heard, again disputing with court ministers, therefore the assembly had nothing to overthrow him with.
translations.idiomatic: Friends warned Gu Yuezhi against memorializing for Yin Hao, but he insisted and won the debate.

sentences.zh: 時人咸稱之。

translations.literal: Men of the time all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised his courage.

sentences.zh: 為州別駕，曆尚書右丞，卒。

translations.literal: He was provincial chief administrator on separate carriage, passed through right aide in the secretariat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as provincial chief administrator and right aide in the secretariat before his death.

sentences.zh: 子凱之，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Kaizhi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu Kaizhi has his own biography in this history.

sentences.zh: 蔡裔者，有勇氣，聲若雷震。

translations.literal: Cai Yi by nature had courage; his voice was like thunderclap.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yi was famed for a shout like thunder.

sentences.zh: 嘗有二偷入室，裔拊床一呼，而盜俱隕，故浩委以軍鋒焉。

translations.literal: Once when two thieves entered the house, Yi slapped the couch once shouting, and both robbers fell dead; therefore Hao entrusted him with the army's van.
translations.idiomatic: Two burglars once dropped dead when he roared from his couch—why Yin Hao made him a vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陸曄等並以時望國華，效彰曆試，迭居端揆，參掌機衡。

translations.literal: The historian says: Lu Ye and the like all by timely reputation were flower of the state, their efficacy shining in successive trials, in rotation occupied the ministerial summit, joined in grasping the pivot and steelyard.
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes that Lu Ye, He Chong, Chu Se, Cai Mo, Zhuge Hui, and Yin Hao were men of national stature who reached the highest councils.

sentences.zh: 然皆率由舊章，得免祗悔。

translations.literal: Yet all followed old statutes and so escaped shameful regret.
translations.idiomatic: Most governed conservatively and avoided grave error.

sentences.zh: 而充抗言孺子，雖屈壓於權臣，翊奉儲君，竟導揚於末命，頻參大議，屢畫嘉謀，可謂忠貞在斯而已。

translations.literal: Yet Chong spoke bluntly to the child heir—though bent under power ministers, he assisted and upheld the heir apparent and in the end guided the final charge, repeatedly joining great deliberations and many times sketching fine plans—this can be called loyalty and purity resting herein alone.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong alone spoke truth to power over the imperial succession and served three emperors faithfully.

sentences.zh: 殷浩清徽雅量，眾議攸歸，高秩厚禮，不行而至，咸謂教義由其興替，社稷俟以安危。

translations.literal: Yin Hao was pure emblem and cultivated capacity; public deliberation turned to him; high rank and thick gifts came without his seeking—all said doctrine and teaching rose or fell through him, the altars waited on him for safety or danger.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao's charisma made the realm expect him to save or sink the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及其入處國鈞，未有嘉謀善政，出總戎律，唯聞蹙國喪師，是知風流異貞固之才，談論非奇正之要。

translations.literal: Yet when he entered to hold the state's spring and presided over no fine plans or good government, when he went out to oversee military law one only heard of shrinking the state and losing armies—thus one knows that refined bearing differs from steadfast talent, and discourse is not the crux of odd versus straight strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he bungled civil and military duties—proving salon brilliance is not statecraft.

sentences.zh: 違方易任，以致播遷，悲失！

translations.literal: Contrary to the proper square, easy change of charge, thereby bringing on wandering removal—sad failure!
translations.idiomatic: Misplaced trust in him brought disaster—sad indeed.

sentences.zh: 蔡謨度德而處，弘斯止足，置以刑書，斯為過矣。

translations.literal: Cai Mo measured virtue and dwelt accordingly, magnifying this doctrine of knowing when to stop; to place him in penal texts was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo knew his limits; punishing him harshly was excessive.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：士光時望，士瑤允當。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Shiguang's timely reputation, Shiyao's trustworthiness balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Shiguang's fame, Shiyao's steady grace.

sentences.zh: 政既弟兄，任惟台相。

translations.literal: Government rested on brothers; office fell to chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers shared government; ministers anchored the state.

sentences.zh: 祖言簡率，遺風可尚。

translations.literal: Zuyan's plain candor left conduct to admire.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na's blunt honesty set a tone worth emulating.

sentences.zh: 蔡葛知名，或雅或清。

translations.literal: Cai and Ge won renown—one cultivated, one clear.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo and Zhuge Hui shone—one refined, one lucid.

sentences.zh: 次道方概，謀遠忠貞。

translations.literal: Cidao's square bearing, Mouyuan's loyal plan.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong stood firm; Chu Se planned deep and true.

sentences.zh: 中軍鑒局，譽光雅俗。

translations.literal: The central army read the board; his praise lit refined and vulgar alike.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao read the game—his fame lit court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 夷曠有餘，經綸不足。

translations.literal: Broad and free he had surplus; ordering the realm he fell short.
translations.idiomatic: He had breadth but not the rope to rule.

sentences.zh: 舍長任短，功虧名辱。

translations.literal: He set aside his length and used his shortness—merit lost, name shamed.
translations.idiomatic: He played his weakness as strength—merit undone, honor ruined.
